claim: GSE owns its expected-value metrics instead of re-serving Next Gen Stats: GSE-CPOE, GSE-RYOE, and GSE-xYAC are computed from public nflverse play-by-play (CC-BY-4.0) with GSE's own feature contracts and coefficients fit at load time. NGS numbers enter the system only as the y-axis of a validation correlation (the referee) and are never copied into a served metric. If code and docs disagree, the code wins.

All three expected metrics share one shape: fit an expected-value model on a season of plays, take the per-play residual (actual minus expected), and roll it up per player into an over-expected rate. The rollup reports per-play means scaled to match NGS units plus an unscaled overExpectedTotal counting stat, sorted descending and id-tiebroken for deterministic output. The join key throughout is the nflverse gsis_id.

GSE-CPOE (model gse-xcomp-v1) is completion percentage over expectation for a passer over qualifying dropbacks: 100 times the mean of (complete minus predicted completion probability), reported in completion-percentage points (reportScale = 100). The estimator is L2-regularized logistic regression by full-batch gradient descent on log-loss over standardized features, with the intercept as a separate unpenalized bias initialized at the class-prior log-odds; defaults 400 iterations, learning rate 0.3, L2 = 1e-3, deterministic (same plays give same coefficients). The 10 canonical features in order are airYards, airYardsSquared, qbHit, isMiddle, isLeft, down, ydstogo, yardline100, shotgun, noHuddle: airYards and its square capture pass depth and its curvature (completion probability falls off nonlinearly with depth); qbHit is the public pressure proxy (qb_hit); isMiddle/isLeft one-hot throw location with right as the reference category. Sample floors: MIN_DROPBACKS_TO_FIT = 200 to fit at all; DEFAULT_MIN_PASSER_ATTEMPTS = 100 for a passer to appear in the rollup.

GSE-RYOE (model gse-xrush-v1) fits its rush-expectation model with closed-form ridge (L2) linear regression: beta = (Z^T Z + lambda R)^{-1} Z^T y computed on a standardized design matrix with a leading intercept column, where R = diag(0, 1, 1, ...) leaves the intercept unpenalized; solved exactly by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, no iteration and no randomness, default lambda = 1.

GSE-RYOE (model gse-xrush-v1) is rush yards over expected per attempt for a rusher over qualifying carries: the mean of (rushingYards minus predicted rushing yards), reported in yards over expected per attempt (reportScale = 1). The 9 canonical features in order are yardline100, down, ydstogo, shotgun, scoreDifferential, runMiddle, runLeft, gapGuard, gapTackle: runMiddle/runLeft one-hot run location with right as reference; gapGuard/gapTackle one-hot run gap with end as reference; scoreDifferential (offense minus defense at snap) captures game-script effects on box counts and run-blocking intent. Sample floors: MIN_RUSHES_TO_FIT = 200; DEFAULT_MIN_RUSHER_ATTEMPTS = 50.

GSE-xYAC (model gse-xyac-v1) is yards after catch over expectation for a receiver over qualifying receptions: the mean of (yardsAfterCatch minus predicted YAC), reported in YAC over expected per catch (reportScale = 1). The estimator is ridge linear regression (same kernel as GSE-RYOE), default lambda = 1. The 6 canonical features in order are airYards, yardline100, down, ydstogo, isMiddle, isLeft: airYards is the dominant public proxy for expected YAC because short in-stride catches carry more YAC potential than deep contested ones; isMiddle/isLeft one-hot throw location with right as reference. Sample floors: MIN_CATCHES_TO_FIT = 200; DEFAULT_MIN_RECEIVER_CATCHES = 30.

The expected-metrics models are fit on load, never hardcoded: the loader fetches a real season of nflverse play-by-play column-projected to only the ~27 columns the three models read, tries [season, season-1] so an empty current season falls back to the most recent complete one, and fits its own models on that exact season. Every fitted model carries provenance: modelVersion (gse-xcomp-v1 / gse-xrush-v1 / gse-xyac-v1, bumped when features change), method (logistic-regression or ridge-linear), ordered featureKeys, featureSchemaHash (a deterministic djb2 hash of featureKeys, 8 hex chars, a drift detector not a cryptographic hash — a changed feature list changes the hash), and sampleSize. Honesty gates return null and emit an empty block rather than guessing: below the 200-play MIN_*_TO_FIT floor; fitLogistic on degenerate labels (all completions or all incompletions, no decision boundary estimable); fitRidge when underdetermined (n < p + 1) or singular even after ridging; on source error the loader returns status source-error with empty blocks.

Validation joins GSE's per-player over-expected series to NGS's on the shared gsis_id and reports agreement via buildCalibrationReport(ours, truth): n (inner-join size), pearson, spearman, rmse, mae, bias defined as ourMean minus truthMean (the systematic offset), ourMean, truthMean. A join of fewer than 2 players yields an all-zero report (no correlation estimable) rather than NaN; all statistics round to 4 decimals. graduationVerdict grades graduated | provisional | insufficient-sample | failed on Pearson with DEFAULT_GRADUATION_THRESHOLDS: cpoe {minSample 12, graduatedPearson 0.60, provisionalPearson 0.35}, xyac {12, 0.50, 0.25}, ryoe {12, 0.40, 0.20}; logic: n < minSample gives insufficient-sample, pearson >= graduatedPearson gives graduated, provisionalPearson <= pearson < graduatedPearson gives provisional, otherwise failed.

The graduation bars are deliberately different because they reflect how much tracking signal is recoverable from public play-by-play: CPOE's bar is high (0.60) because completion probability is mostly pass depth plus pressure, both publicly available (air yards, its square, qb_hit); xYAC's bar is medium (0.50) because YAC is strongly air-yards-driven (public) but also depends on defender proximity at the catch point (tracking-only); RYOE's bar is lower (0.40) because expected rush yards leans hardest on defenders-in-the-box and runner closing/top speed, exactly the tracking geometry public data cannot see.

Grain discipline is the top correctness rule: a Pearson correlation between two per-player series is only meaningful at identical aggregation grain, which requires all four of: same season (the season PBP actually resolved to, activeSeason, after the [season, season-1] fallback, not the requested season blindly), same season type (REG only on both sides), same per-player key (nflverse gsis_id joined 1:1), and matched per-player qualifiers (season-aggregate per player on both sides; the NGS side read from week-0 season-aggregate rows filtered week == 0, season_type == REG, season == activeSeason; the join is an inner join so only players qualifying on both sides enter). Lethal mistakes this forbids: correlating a per-play series against a per-season series, a min-100-attempt pool against a min-1 pool, REG against REG+POST, or joining on name instead of gsis_id — each silently produces a meaningless correlation.

NGS is fit on optical/RFID player tracking — (x, y) position and velocity of all 22 players at ~10 Hz — giving its private models signals physically absent from public play-by-play: receiver separation and cushion at the throw and catch, defender proximity at the catch point, defenders-in-the-box and the pre-snap front, runner closing speed / top speed / time-to-line-of-scrimmage, and time-to-throw plus route geometry. GSE's public proxies are coarser by construction: air_yards (and its square), qb_hit as a binary pressure flag, throw/run location and run gap buckets, down/distance/field position, shotgun/no-huddle, and score differential — recovering some of the tracking signal (a lot for CPOE, less for RYOE) but not all, which is why the graduation bars are set where they are.

Defensible-claims boundary: GSE can claim its metrics are its own (own feature contract, coefficients fit on public data at load time, provenance-stamped and auditable) and that at matched grain its per-player values reproduce the NGS ranking and level to the degree the calibration report shows (Pearson and Spearman with RMSE/MAE/bias, graded by a pre-registered threshold per metric). It cannot claim identity with NGS's model (different inputs by construction), cannot claim its number equals the NGS number for a player (bias in the report is the standing reminder of the systematic offset), and cannot claim anything forward-looking: GSE Expected Metrics are historical measurement, canPublishProjections stays false, and wiring into the edge/scoring engine is a separate founder-gated MODEL_VERSION step, not an automatic consequence of a graduated verdict.

Expected Points (model gse-ep-v1) is estimated with seven one-vs-rest binary logistics over the next-score outcome, renormalized to a distribution — there is no softmax and no multinomial fitter in the codebase; EP reuses the existing binary logistic. Play type is any non-terminal down-to-down state; features are down, ydstogo, yardline100, yardline100Squared, goalToGo, halfSecondsRemaining. Outcomes and values in the possession frame are TD +7, FG +3, SAFETY +2, NONE 0, OPP_SAFETY -2, OPP_FG -3, OPP_TD -7, and EP(state) equals the sum over outcomes k of P(next-score = k) times value(k), provably in [-7, 7] as a convex combination of values in [-7, 7].

EPA is EP(after) minus EP(before); on a possession change EP(after) is in the opponent's frame, so it is negated to return to the before-team's frame. Rare-head graceful degradation: the required heads {TD, FG, NONE, OPP_FG, OPP_TD} must fit or no surface is served; the rare safety heads (SAFETY, OPP_SAFETY) may fail to fit and a null head contributes raw probability 0 before renormalization, keeping EP bounded. TD = 7 is a v1 simplification inclusive of the expected PAT; a future gse-ep-v2 may adopt the PAT-adjusted ~6.95 value. Sample floor: MIN_EP_PLAYS_TO_FIT = 1000 usable plays, below which the fit returns null.

Win Probability (model gse-wp-v1) is a single binary logistic of P(the possession team ultimately wins): WP(state) = sigma(beta dot features), already in the open interval (0, 1) with no clamp applied. Features are scoreDifferential, gameSecondsRemaining, scoreDiffPerSqrtTime, yardline100, down, ydstogo, timeoutDifferential, spreadLine. WPA is WP(after) minus WP(before); on a possession change WP(after) is the opponent's win probability, so it is replaced by its complement 1 - WP(after). A missing market spread is imputed as spreadLine = 0 (a pick'em), which conflates 'missing' with a genuine pick'em and is an accepted v1 imputation. Sample floor: MIN_WP_PLAYS_TO_FIT = 1000.
WPA is WP(after) minus WP(before); on a possession change the after value is the opponent's win probability and must be complemented as 1 - WP(after) before differencing.

Success rate (model gse-success-v1) is a deterministic rule with no fit: a play is a success if it is a touchdown (forced) OR (not a turnover AND yards gained >= fraction(down) * yards-to-go), with SUCCESS_YARDAGE_FRACTION = {1: 0.4, 2: 0.6, 3: 1.0, 4: 1.0}. Precedence: a turnover forces failure and dominates a touchdown flag (a pick-six is a turnover, hence an offensive failure). An unratable down (not in {1,2,3,4}) returns null and is dropped from every count — the down is range-guarded before indexing the fraction table so the lookup is always a real number. Splits are by team, player, down, and early/late by short/medium/long situation bucket; there is no 'over expected' surface in v1.

Drives (model gse-drives-v1) is pure drive segmentation with a test-enforced partition-completeness invariant: every input play lands in exactly one drive, the sum of playCount equals plays.length, and the multiset of playIds is preserved — no play dropped, duplicated, or invented. Two modes: explicit driveId grouping, or detect-by-possession-change with synthesized sequential ids; an empty-posteam play attaches to the open drive and an empty-posteam first play starts a drive (never orphaned). Result classification: an explicit terminalOutcome is authoritative; otherwise points >= 6 means TD, points == 3 means FG, else OTHER — and a safety is never inferred from a point total since a safety is scored by the defense. pointsScored is actual points (TD 6, FG 3, safety 2, PAT/XP 1, two-point 2, 0 otherwise) and must not be mapped from nflfastR's binary sp scoring-play indicator, because an sp mapping would total a TD+PAT drive as 1 + 1 = 2 and misclassify it as OTHER. Aggregates: points (sum), epaTotal (sum of epa ?? 0), successRate over ratable plays only (0, not NaN, when none are ratable), start/end field position from first/last play by playIndex.

EP is proven against nflverse ep, EPA against epa, and WP against wp, all at play grain via buildEpCalibration / buildWpCalibration (thin play-grain helpers reusing the same numeric primitives — Pearson, Spearman, RMSE, MAE, mean — no second statistics kernel). Thresholds: ep {minSample: 200, graduatedPearson: 0.9, provisionalPearson: 0.75}, wp {minSample: 200, graduatedPearson: 0.9, provisionalPearson: 0.8}, where minSample is reinterpreted as paired plays, not players. The bars are high because EP and WP are almost fully functions of the public situation (down / distance / field position / score / time), so a faithful public reconstruction should correlate strongly with the referee. Success rate and drives are definitional — no correlation gate, only determinism and the partition invariant, enforced by unit tests.

EPA validation excludes terminal scoring plays on both sides of the join: v1 EPA covers non-terminal down-to-down transitions only, and the nflverse epa join must be filtered to the identical non-terminal set or the correlation mixes grains. EP/WP validation grain is per-play, same season, same season type (REG), joined on game_id + play_id; never mix seasons.

The two sign conventions are the top correctness hazard and are different operations: EP negates on a possession flip — EP(after) becomes -EP(after) — because it is a signed point expectation; WP complements on a possession flip — WP(after) becomes 1 - WP(after) — because it is a probability in [0, 1]. Treating a WP flip as a negation or an EP flip as a complement is the classic bug. Both expectedPointsAdded and winProbabilityAdded document the after-play possession-frame caller contract: 'after' must be expressed from the after-play possession team's frame.

EP, WP, success rate, and drives are glass-box and enter dark: additive, descriptive, historical metrics that are not wired into scoring.ts, constants.ts, or any confidence/edge math — shipping them changes no served output. They are descriptive and historical, not performance claims (no win rate, no ROI, no profit, no closing-line-value assertion), and wiring any of them into scoring or confidence would require a founder-gated MODEL_VERSION step under the model-freeze guardrail.

Operating law: no number enters GSE unless it can survive cross-examination — grounded in a target question, source-rights-clean, deterministic in code, validated before promotion, exposed through public drivers (not protected weights), and blocked or downgraded when freshness, rights, calibration, drift, or no-bet pressure fails.

A formula conflict was resolved in favor of the newer contract: the doctrine contained an earlier DRI sketch using 0.40/0.25/0.20/0.15 weights plus a separate rights penalty, while the First Build Slice contained the newer DRI contract using 0.38/0.22/0.20/0.20 weights with rights_cleanliness as a direct term; the code implements the First Build Slice formula because it is the explicit build prompt for this slice, and the older doctrine formula is retained only as calibration history for future validation comparison before promotion.

Protected basis expansion makes raw features harder to reverse-engineer: phi(x) = [x, x^2, x^3, max(0, x-k1)^3, max(0, x-k2)^3, max(0, x-k3)^3, log(1 + abs(x)), sigmoid(a*x)], a cubic-spline-style expansion with two knots triples plus a logarithmic and a sigmoidal term.
equation: phi(x) = [x, x^2, x^3, max(0, x−k1)^3, max(0, x−k2)^3, max(0, x−k3)^3, log(1 + abs(x)), sigmoid(a·x)]

claim: Data Reliability Index answers 'is this data reliable enough to influence a decision?' with the implemented Slice 1 formula: freshness_score is 1.00 if age <= 0.5TTL, 0.65 if 0.5TTL < age <= TTL, 0.15 if age > TTL, 0.00 if missing; coverage_score = min(1, source_count / expected_source_count); rights_cleanliness is 1.00 if approved/allowed, 0.60 if benchmark_only/manual_review/restricted, 0.00 if permission_required/blocked/excluded/unknown; contradiction_penalty = min(0.50, 0.20 * contradiction_count); missing_penalty = min(0.40, 0.08 * missing_required_fields); and DRI = 100 * clamp(0.38*freshness_score + 0.22*coverage_score + 0.20*provider_trust_score + 0.20*rights_cleanliness - contradiction_penalty - missing_penalty, 0, 1). Output grades are HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, BLOCKED; DRI feeds no-bet pressure, API warnings, and content approval.
equation:
freshness_score =
  1.00 if age <= 0.5TTL
  0.65 if 0.5TTL < age <= TTL
  0.15 if age > TTL
  0.00 if missing

coverage_score = min(1, source_count / expected_source_count)

rights_cleanliness =
  1.00 if approved/allowed
  0.60 if benchmark_only/manual_review/restricted
  0.00 if permission_required/blocked/excluded/unknown

contradiction_penalty = min(0.50, 0.20 * contradiction_count)
missing_penalty = min(0.40, 0.08 * missing_required_fields)

DRI =
  100 * clamp(
    0.38*freshness_score
  + 0.22*coverage_score
  + 0.20*provider_trust_score
  + 0.20*rights_cleanliness
  - contradiction_penalty
  - missing_penalty,
  0, 1)

claim: Market Gravity Index answers 'is the market meaningfully pulling toward a side, total, or prop?' using line movement, book consensus, timing, injury explainability, key-number crossing, staleness, and dispersion. Stale data cannot be classified as a clean market signal — it returns NO_SIGNAL. It is derived market interpretation, not raw odds resale; it exposes score, stale flag, signal band, and drivers but not market-normalization weights, timing decay calibration, the key-number table, or injury explainability logic; and it is not an edge claim — injury-explained movement and key-number crossings can support classification but never prove value.

Stale Line Risk Score answers 'is this line too stale, thin, contradictory, or rights-unclear to support market interpretation?' It is a market-risk score, not a playable-edge score — higher is worse — using line age, freshness TTL, source coverage, contradiction pressure, source-rights cleanliness, book dispersion, and movement audit pressure. A line snapshot at or beyond the freshness TTL is forced to BLOCK and marketSignalAllowed becomes false even when the line moved sharply. It complements Market Gravity: MGI asks whether the market is pulling; SLRS asks whether the line snapshot is trustworthy enough to interpret; and no stale line is ever classified as a clean market signal.

Market Mirage Score answers 'is the apparent market signal real enough for downstream review, or is it likely a noisy, stale, narrative-driven, contradictory, or source-weak mirage?' It is a market-risk score — not win probability, expected value, betting advice, or a pick trigger — and higher is worse. It composes Market Gravity, Stale Line Risk Score, market-signal allowance, public narrative heat, source contradiction pressure, book dispersion, market explainability, no-bet pressure, drift pressure, calibration debt, and source-policy posture. probability is always null; confidenceScore measures evidence quality, not edge, probability, advice quality, or pick strength. Stale or blocked market signals, blocked source-policy posture, high no-bet pressure, high drift pressure, or high calibration debt block market interpretation before downstream review.

GSE Signal Score answers 'is this signal high-quality enough to act on?' It is a decision-quality score, not win probability: probability is always null and confidenceMeaning is DECISION_QUALITY_NOT_WIN_PROBABILITY. It combines edge quality, signal integrity, market gravity, proprietary player signal, calibration integrity, portfolio fit, no-bet pressure, drift pressure, calibration debt, and interaction penalties; no-bet pressure, drift pressure, and calibration debt are suppressors, not decorative drivers. Public output includes grade, score, confidence score, and sorted drivers — not protected weights or interaction coefficients. Public grades: HARD_PASS, PASS, WATCH, LEAN, SPEAK, STRONG.

Metric graduation statuses are BLOCKED_SOURCE_RIGHTS, BLOCKED_MODEL_CARD, BLOCKED_SAMPLE, BLOCKED_VALIDATION, BLOCKED_DRIFT, REVIEW_READY, APPROVED_FOR_CONTENT, APPROVED_FOR_API, enforced in pure TypeScript: a missing source-rights envelope blocks; a source with mayUseForModeling=false blocks all graduation; API exposure blocks when any source has mayExposeDerived=false; sample size below threshold blocks; a missing model card blocks; validation status other than PASS blocks; missing or severe drift blocks; SHADOW metrics can reach content-aggregate approval only after gates pass; SHADOW metrics cannot be exposed through API routes; full API exposure requires all gates plus a non-shadow approved metric asset.

Source-rights policy boundary: nflverse is approved_open_license — allowed for modeling, validation, and derived metrics with attribution, raw API blocked by default; the-odds-api is approved_api — blocked for model training because the web registry sets model_training_allowed=false, allowed for validation and for derived market intelligence where the payload does not expose raw provider values, raw API blocked. Raw odds fields, protected weights, and unknown-source fields fail closed for API payloads; public drivers and aggregate derived scores are allowed only when every referenced source permits the requested exposure. This layer is a code-level policy gate, not a legal clearance claim.

The receiving/rushing Slice 1 metrics follow the same foundation rules (SHADOW lifecycle, birth certificate, public drivers not protected weights, confidence as evidence quality, source-policy carried through): Receiver Difficulty Index rises when expected completion probability falls, air yards rise, separation/cushion proxies worsen, or contested-catch and sideline proxies rise, and shrinks the receiver prior difficulty toward neutral at low sample; Expected YAC rises with space, separation, cushion, and a shrunk receiver YAC prior and falls with defender leverage, deeper target depth, and red-zone constraint; YAC Creation starts from the residual between actual YAC and expected-yac-gse, rising when actual YAC clears the baseline and falling when it underperforms, using the receiver YAC-over-expected prior as a shrinkage stabilizer; Rush Environment Index describes the rushing context before crediting or blaming the ball carrier, rising with lighter box pressure, stronger offensive-line continuity, favorable run-direction leverage, and run-friendly game script, falling with heavy box/front pressure, worse down-distance stress, and weather penalty; Expected Rush Yards starts from rush-environment-index rather than copying any private expected-rush output; Rush Over Expected starts from the residual between actual rushing yards and expected-rush-yards-gse. The Player Residual Rollup helper rolls yac-creation-gse and rush-over-expected-gse play-level residuals into player-season summaries grouped only by metric, player, and season (direct mixed rollups are rejected, not blended), returning SHADOW/INTERNAL summaries only.

The validation ladder for any metric is: directional unit test, synthetic fixture test, historical walk-forward, segment calibration, baseline comparison, drift report, shadow board impact, then public/API approval. No metric leaves SHADOW without a model card, source card, validation card, and drift card.

Cross-cutting confidence semantics: confidenceScore always measures evidence quality — never probability, win probability, expected value, edge, or certainty. This applies to expected completion, QB Burden Index, Role Volatility Index, Calibration Integrity Grade, Drift Pressure Index, Conformal Uncertainty Width, No-Bet Pressure, Playable Window Score, Portfolio Fit Score, Market Mirage Score, and GSE Signal Score. For the market and decision metrics, probability is always null. QB Burden Index is contextual burden (not quarterback quality); Role Volatility Index is role instability (not player quality); blocked source-policy posture forces BLOCKED modeling posture with high uncertainty.

The GSE Score Engine is a shadow-only decision-quality layer: it is not wired into live output generation, does not change production scoring, and does not claim calibrated win probability by itself. It separates five concepts that must not be collapsed: modeled probability (the model parliament's estimate for the side under review), confidence score (decision quality from model agreement, vote quality, and evidence health), feature contract (whether required inputs, source policy, and freshness survive), calibration contract (whether probability language is earned), and no-bet strength (how strongly the system should refuse action). The final GSE Action Score is a 0-100 decision-quality index, not a win probability.

Score Engine guardrails: missing required data can force HARD_PASS; stale required data can force HARD_PASS while stale optional data remains a warning; source-rights blocks can force HARD_PASS; high expected value cannot override hard-pass data gaps; model disagreement reduces confidence and increases no-bet pressure; stale data increases no-bet pressure; calibration claims are blocked unless the calibration contract is validated; outputs expose drivers, not internal protected weights.

The Score Engine's decision labels are shadow-only decision-quality classifications, not action recommendations: PLAY means the shadow score clears the local quality gates; LEAN means positive but not strong enough for a hard action recommendation; WATCH means needs monitoring because evidence is incomplete or not yet strong; PASS means no-bet pressure or low score suppresses action; HARD_PASS means missing data, source rights, responsible-gaming, or another hard block prevents action.

Shadow metric evidence reports are generated from synthetic/local evidence fixtures and prove local governance behavior only; they do not approve public content, API exposure, licensing, betting use, production promotion, legal clearance, or metric lifecycle graduation. Shared locks on every report: shadow-only lifecycle, API exposure INTERNAL, licensing NOT_READY, public API exposure disabled, live route creation disabled, evidence labeled synthetic/local, and no probability, expected-value, pick, or betting-advice claim is created by any report.

Ten shadow metrics carry DRAFT model cards (status, not readiness) and drift cards computed as named delta metrics against watch/severe thresholds: stale-line-risk-score WATCH (market_freshness_psi 0.18 vs watch 0.15 / severe 0.30); qb-burden-index STABLE (burden_distribution_psi 0.08 vs 0.14 / 0.28); role-volatility-index WATCH (role_stability_psi 0.21 vs 0.16 / 0.32); calibration-integrity-grade WATCH (calibration_integrity_ece_delta 0.07 vs 0.05 / 0.12); drift-pressure-index WATCH (drift_pressure_composite_delta 0.16 vs 0.12 / 0.28); conformal-uncertainty-width WATCH (conformal_width_coverage_gap_delta 0.13 vs 0.08 / 0.24); no-bet-pressure WATCH (no_bet_hard_pass_rate_delta 0.17 vs 0.12 / 0.28); playable-window-score SEVERE (decision_window_block_rate_delta 0.31 vs 0.12 / 0.25); portfolio-fit-score STABLE (portfolio_concentration_risk_delta 0.11 vs 0.16 / 0.30); market-mirage-score WATCH (market_mirage_watch_rate_delta 0.19 vs 0.14 / 0.28). Drift status STABLE/WATCH/SEVERE is a threshold comparison of a synthetic-fixture delta, not production drift evidence.

A Brier score on its own is not a claim about skill: the pregame context bridge's Brier of 0.223743 on the 2025 holdout (285 games) is only good or bad relative to what you would have got by predicting the base rate, so the audit compared it against baselines (always-predict-base-rate 0.249848, always-predict-0.5 0.250000).

The pregame context bridge on the 2025 holdout (285 games): model Brier 0.223743 vs base-rate Brier 0.249848 (training home-win base rate 0.564297 over 6,991 rows, 1999-2024), log loss 0.636548, and 10-bin ECE 0.051868; the evaluation is out-of-sample by construction because scripts/run-bridge.mjs trains only on seasons strictly before 2025 and scores 2025 only.

Brier skill vs the base rate is +0.026190 with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [+0.010734, +0.041393] from 10,000 paired resamples (seed 20260927), and P(skill > 0) = 0.9997; because the interval excludes zero, the skill is not noise.

Reasoning about the bootstrap design: the resampling is paired over games because the model and the base rate are scored on the same game, so the difference between the two scores is far better determined than either score alone.

Measured verdict: the market-to-confidence leak is real, confirmed, and quantified - published confidence moves 7 points when a market probability changes and nothing about the recommended bet changes at all (this was a measurement, no production code was changed).

The leak is by design and documented in the source: scoring.ts:1219 states 'Heuristic confidence stays as the market-echo composite for UX continuity', so the remediation is a labelling problem rather than a bug fix - a number that is partly the book is being presented to users as confidence.

Contamination channel 1 (spread side): scoring.ts:510-521 computes fairProb = removeVig(homeImpliedAvg, awayImpliedAvg) - the same quantity the receipt commits as marketFairProb - which flows into computeEdgeScore (scoring.ts:532, body :310-344) and is added into the confidence sum at scoring.ts:580-588.

Contamination channel 2 (H2H moneyline): scoring.ts:540-547 computes mlFairProbHome = removeVig(avgH, avgA) and passes it to computeCrossMarketScore (game-context.ts:698, body :451-490), which returns plus/minus CROSS_MARKET_AGREE_BONUS (4) or CROSS_MARKET_DISAGREE_PENALTY (3) (constants.ts:79,81), added into the same confidence sum at scoring.ts:573 and :584; there is also a third-order path through computeUncertaintyPenalty consuming crossMarketScore (game-context.ts:597).

The isolation measurement held entry price, line, book count, teams, and selection identical and varied only a market probability: channel 1 (marketFairProb 0.5000 -> 0.3957) moved confidence 57 -> 50 with a byte-identical bet; channel 2 (H2H agrees -> opposes) moved confidence 61 -> 54 with a byte-identical bet (test suite: 4 passed).

Because the de-vig is proportional, symmetric repricing barely moves the edge term - you must move the opposing side's price at a fixed entry price to move marketFairProb, which is the isolation the fixture uses, and the fixture guards itself against passing vacuously.

Test-design reasoning for documenting known bugs: three of the four tests are it.fails asserting the current leaky behaviour, because committing them as ordinary it() would leave the branch permanently red (which teaches people to ignore red); the suite stays green while the leak stands and flips red the moment someone fixes it, and that red is the signal to delete the guards; the fourth test is a plain passing it() pinning the leak's magnitude (>= 5 points), and if it ever fails the leak was repaired.

The calibration page ('The Proof Room', a live route) is dark and confirmed dark via a fail-closed gate on every path (stub mode false, load error false, PERFORMANCE_STATS_ENABLED read with default false), the live production value is NOT_EVALUATED, and the named missing env var is PERFORMANCE_STATS_ENABLED; nothing was enabled and no win-rate, ROI, or units figure was created.

Product-surface implication: any analysis of 'does high confidence win more?' is for this number partly measuring the book, which restates the standing prohibition on publishing a bucket table of public win rates; the calibration page staying dark is what stands between this and a published claim the market has already made.

Remediation restraint: the production scorer was deliberately not patched because removing the two market channels changes every downstream surface, that is a product decision rather than an overnight measurement, and scoring.ts is a shared hot path the parallel session also reads - this slice measures, it does not decide.

Drive-start field position (first snap of each drive from nflverse play-by-play) was calibrated with 2025 as the prior and 2026 weeks 1-2 shrunk with k=12 drives: correlation versus 2025 home win +0.186, slope +0.0647, standard error 0.0208, n=272, and the signal is LIVE. In the drive-start calibration, a lower starting yardline_100 means closer to the end zone, so the signed helper (away start minus home start, divided by 4) measures which team starts drives with better field position.

The Hugging Face embedding failure was root-caused to a monthly Inference Providers spending limit, not a mystery: the hosted bge-m3 call returned HTTP 403 'You have exceeded your monthly spending limit for Inference Providers.' The storage/compute/egress dashboard read $0.00 because those meters are separate from the Inference Providers budget, which is a ceiling rather than a charge; nothing unauthorized was being charged. Not established: the actual dollar figure, the cap, and the reset date, because HF exposes no readable balance API (billing overview and credits endpoints both return 404).

The Hugging Face token diagnosis found the founder's pasted token had a dropped character and duplication (74 characters supplied; HF tokens are 37); both the raw 74-char paste and a naive de-duplication to 38 chars returned 401 'Invalid username or password', while the correct 37-char form returned 200 on GET /api/whoami-v2.

The legacy Hugging Face endpoint api-inference.huggingface.co no longer resolves (HTTP 000) because that hostname is retired; a pipeline pointed at it fails forever regardless of billing, a distinct problem from the 403 spending-limit signal which is the only alert that matters.

The ordered remedy for the HF billing block is: raise or top up the Inference Providers limit in account billing (self-serve, no ticket needed); point the embedding path at the local bge-m3, already the documented path, and remove any still-wired hosted call since a paid endpoint already exhausted is a standing failure with a monthly cadence; and alert on the 403 specifically.

The HF billing block had no impact on the production embedding path because bge-m3 runs locally as the documented embedding path; nothing in production depends on the hosted endpoint, which is why the block was never on the critical path and stayed undiagnosed.

The walk-forward methodology scores each season only with a model fit on earlier seasons, and 2026 data neither chose the home-field constant nor entered the 2015-2025 fits.

Weighted across 2015-2025 on the games where all three models exist, Elo scored Brier 0.2314, the pregame logit scored 0.2262, and the devigged price scored 0.2122, so the devigged price is the sharpest of the three; a lower Brier means a sharper probability.

The Neon production endpoint ep-summer-moon-apv5ccys was changed via the Neon API from autoscaling_limit_max_cu 8 to 1 and from unset to suspend_timeout_seconds 300, verified by a separate GET rather than the PATCH response because a write that returns its own input is not a verification; the Neon API requires the body under an 'endpoint' key, and suspend_timeout_seconds sits on the endpoint rather than the compute, since setting it on the compute binding returns 200 and changes nothing.

The Neon project has 42 endpoints, every one at autoscaling_limit_max_cu 8, and only the production endpoint was changed; 41 are preview/pr-* branches, and at 8 CU the worst case per always-awake branch is 8 x 0.106 x 730 = $618.92/mo versus ~$19.35/mo at the 0.25 CU floor, which is the quantified form of the cost doctrine that every forgotten branch is another ~$19/mo leak.

The brief's $60.84/mo figure rests on 574 active hours, which is an assumption rather than a measurement: it presumes the compute is awake 23.9 hours per day, whereas if the 23 Vercel crons keep hitting the DB roughly every 2 minutes the compute never suspends and the real figure is the floor of 0.25 x 0.106 x 730 = $19.35/mo. The honest summary is that $60.84/mo is the ceiling this configuration makes impossible to exceed, not a predicted bill, and the worst case also assumes the autoscale actually pins at 1 CU, which no measured peak confirms.

The 1 CU cap is justified by the tail, not the steady state: from the round-2 audit at Launch pricing of $0.106/CU-hr, a 48-hour runaway costs $81.41 at 16 CU unbounded versus $10.18 at the 1 CU cap and $5.09 at 0.5 CU, so the cap is insurance against one bad backfill or parallelizing query, and 1 CU is wide enough for the small read-heavy SELECT workload on the 33,962-row table.

Still open on the Neon infrastructure: the plan tier is unconfirmed (the billing screenshot reviewed earlier was Vercel's, not Neon's, and every dollar figure assumes Launch pricing); no spend alert is confirmed on; the 41 preview branches remain uncapped because bulk-writing them was a state-changing action outside the brief; and no production query was run to confirm a peak CU, so the cap is set from doctrine rather than measured workload.

For NGS summary tables from nflverse (passing, rushing, receiving) through 2026 week 2, a component went live in week 3 only when its same-season correlation with the 2025 home result had |r| of at least 0.08: LIVE were NGS CPOE (n=255, r=+0.176), time to throw (r=+0.110), air yards differential (r=+0.184), rush yards over expected (r=+0.124), and YAC over expected (r=+0.171); stored but unused were aggressiveness (r=-0.057), separation (r=+0.010), and special-teams EPA from play-by-play (n=272, r=+0.054).

The 2025 r values used to gate NGS components into the week-3 edge are same-season associations, not a week-lagged walk-forward: they decide what is allowed to inform week 3 and are not a claim that NGS beats the market close.

NGS doctrine in this engine: Next Gen summary tables are ingested to learn and are not treated as a stolen commercial feed -- raw RFID tracking, PFF grades, and SIS charting stay out; NGS may move on-field efficiency by at most 0.15 of that family's signed value, and it cannot replace the opponent-adjusted EPA blend nor decide the game.

Offensive-line drag was fitted on 1,069 team-weeks in 2024-2025, where the outcome is points scored minus what that opponent usually allows and each team is compared with itself: a missing starting tackle (129 games, -2.65 points, se 0.91) is used at -2.61 (multiplier -0.1132); a tackle who did not practice (87 games, -1.77, se 1.20) is used at -1.72 (-0.0746); a limited starting tackle (154 games, -1.17, se 0.90) is used at -1.15 (-0.0498); an out interior lineman (+0.95, se 0.98) and an out backup tackle (37 games, -0.52, se 1.58) are both stored as zero. Doubtful is pooled with out, and a questionable tag is not the input -- the input is whether the starting tackle practiced.
The OL-drag shrinkage rule: a fitted coefficient noisier than 7 points is pulled toward zero, and a coefficient inside one standard error -- or a positive one -- is stored as zero rather than used.

Operon is the C++ symbolic-regression library from HEAL (Burlacu, Kronberger, Kommenda, GECCO 2020; Python is pyoperon) and it leads accuracy on many SRBench black-box sets because it runs nonlinear least squares -- Levenberg-Marquardt with automatic differentiation -- on the numeric constants inside every candidate tree, not because it has wiser operators than gplearn: a tree that is almost right gets a fair error, while a sin-sqrt-min costume that only worked because its constants were frozen at genetic values gets exposed.

Operon has no built-in LogitMarginLoss objective, so scoring drive scored-versus-not-scored as an R-squared regression on a 0/1 label is only honest as a ranking check; running it as a classification objective without recoding the label or wrapping a custom objective is the same class of mistake as MOVE-37.

Operon's role in the repo is a ceiling check, not a week-3 signal: given a fast local-search GP, the question is whether any short formula beats the two-feature identity already measured at AUC 0.604 -- read the Pareto front and keep the shortest model whose holdout AUC is within epsilon of the best; if that model is an affine function of yardline and ydstogo, Operon agrees with the ablation and nothing new enters the tilt, and if no short formula beats the identity, MOVE-37 is closed. Never paste an Operon tree into engine-reading.mjs just because SRBench says Operon wins on average -- the holdout on 2024-2025 drives is the only number that matters.

Operon's default symbols are add, sub, mul, div, constant, and variable, with extra symbols available (fmin, fmax, aq, pow, abs, sin, cos, tanh, exp, log); for the Target B rerun trigonometric symbols are left off, the multi-objective front optimizes r2 and length under NSGA-II, and the default single objective is r2.

The scalarizer is the only way a number becomes LIVE in this engine: f1=0 when |r|>=0.08 AND |slope|>se (otherwise DARK); f2=1 when that direction already has a representative in parts-registry.jsonl (duplication is DARK); f3=1 when the week-3 row for the game is missing (STORED when the fit is real); lambda=(0.5,0.3,0.2), g=max(lambda_i * f_i), and g=0 is the only LIVE path; a locked family with no numeric value on a game stays LIVE and contributes 0, which is not STORED.

A DARK family reactivates only when the objective that failed flips: naming a referee does not flip officials, a forecast does not flip weather_physics, nfl4th does not flip coaching, and a contract file existing does not flip narrative_contract -- the flip is a new walk-forward holdout that clears both honesty bars.

A second representative of a family that already has one is a duplicate, not a new signal: pbp CPOE and NGS CPOE are a known duplicate pair, as are schedules.weather with pbp.weather and go-rate with nfl4th; a sibling helper is capped at 0.15 of weight (drive-start is already the helper on scheme), and nfl4th is the sibling of go-rate, not a new coaching part.

Measurement rules in this engine: training rows are seasons 2024 or earlier and the holdout is 2025 -- fitting on 2025 and scoring 2025 is forbidden, and two seasons are not a training set; every fit reports n, Pearson r, OLS slope, and the standard error of that slope, and a correlation without a slope and se cannot pass f1; nulls (for example null punt_wp) are excluded from the regression and counted as excluded while real zeros stay in -- do not drop zeros to inflate r.

Market prices are context, never the objective: never use the market line as a feature and then call the residual an independent edge; calibration meters never become the edge; the tilt equals the engine edge; missing signals add zero; live families are never rescaled so that the weights of the present signals sum to 1; a null value adds its prior to the dark share.

In the prop pricing stack, edge is computed as e = p - q with q from Shin devigging rather than a proportional vig split; pricePropAgainstMarket stays pure with no filesystem import and priced stays false until a decision-time price archive exists and a settlement module the agent did not fake can settle CLV.

claim: Home/away is the sign of the sum of prior times signed -- never pick a side and then change the sign to match it; the reasoning-edge priors sum to 1 with no ninth prior added (efficiency 0.14, scheme 0.12, availability 0.12, schedule 0.08, historical 0.08, weather 0.07, coaching 0.06, trench 0.05, airwave 0.05, officials 0.04, chemistry 0.04, bio_nutrition 0.04, narrative 0.03, social 0, market 0.05, meters 0.03), and the market and meter directions carry context/measurement mass but never enter the tilt.

The edge trace encodes a signed part as 0.5 + 0.49 times clip(signed), which lies inside (0,1) but is not a win probability; signed parts in [-1,1] stay signed in the registry and the 0.5-plus-0.49 encoding must never be stored as if it were the part.

Sure Independence Screening does not stop on a p-value; it stops when growing the subspace stops changing the model, and if the true second descriptor is not in the screened subspace, no later step can recover it.

At dimension n, every constructed feature is scored against the current residual as the correlation of the feature with the previous residual, and the subspace is the k features with the largest absolute score before l0 searches combinations inside it.

The nf_sis (k) knob is a count, not a correlation floor: keep the top k. A correlation floor |w| > tau is usually worse here because correlated pairs like yardline and yards-to-go lose the weaker member even when it is the orthogonal piece the residual needs.

Compressed-sensing scaling from the 2018 paper is a starting guess, not a fitted cutoff: k scales as exp(#P / (kappa n)) with kappa in [1,10], and larger dimension forces a smaller k because l0 is combinatorial.

Operational convergence procedure: fit n=1 at k in {200,500,1000}, record the winning expression and its residual, then fit n=2 at the same k values with one residual then ten residuals; converged means the selected expressions and the holdout residual do not move when k doubles, and that plateau is the threshold.

TorchSISSO's default k=20 is a materials-lab default for tiny N; Target B has tens of thousands of drives, and k=20 can return only field position and look finished while distance never entered the subspace.

Multiple residuals matter: SISSO++ scores each feature as the maximum correlation over the best r residuals, one residual plus a small k is how a correlated second term dies, and fifty residuals recovered a two-term toy that a single residual needed k>400 to see; yardline versus distance is that pair.

Calibration floor as a convergence benchmark: MOVE-37 measured the smooth two-feature identity at AUC 0.604 and the booster at 0.627, so a SISSO model that does not clear 0.604 is under the identity and is not converged.

Stop adding dimension when the next dimension's holdout gain is inside the standard error of the last, or when the new descriptor is an operator costume of the last (for example sin of yardline after yardline is already in).

Tilt admission gate: a signal enters the tilt only if its correlation with home-team winning is above 0.03 in the direction that makes the signal useful; otherwise the number is kept on the row and the family stays dark.

Pressure matchup is the home team's pressure created minus pressure allowed, minus the same net for the away team, where pressure is qb_hit divided by dropbacks; on 2025 walk-forward (250 games) pearson r=0.2414, so it enters the tilt.

Wrong-direction findings are not sign-flipped: special-teams EPA (mean EPA on kickoffs, punts, field goals, extra points) correlated the wrong way at r=-0.0648 on 256 games and was left out, and fourth-down go rate (passes and runs over passes/runs/punts/field goals, r=-0.0136 on 255 games) is recorded but not treated as 'more aggressive is better'.
Methodological rule: the week-3 2026 model was fitted on 7,240 games from seasons before 2026 and this season's results were not in the fit, with settled 2026 games forward Brier 0.2524 on 33 games.

Withheld-means-no-side rule: a game is withheld when the pregame model and the devigged moneyline differ by more than 0.08, and withholding is not a side. Week 3 2026 had 10 association, 6 withheld, 0 insufficient.
Association-only status means the premises name the same outcome and agree, but interference is not cleared, so the read stays an association rather than a causal claim.

The week-3 fantasy edge is built from half-PPR history shrunk toward 2025, then moved by the game composite defined as 1 + 0.08 * team edge; fantasy rank and both DFS solvers spend that model number, not third-party projections.
DST scoring in the week-3 slate build uses sacks, interceptions, fumble recoveries, defensive touchdowns, safeties, and points allowed; yards allowed are not scored.

The week-3 current wire enforces point-in-time integrity: nothing in a snapshot row uses that game's result, so every feature (roster, injury report, coaches, snap counts, team passing EPA, charted play-calls) is strictly as-of prior information.
Charting in the wire is limited to observable flags - motion, play-action, RPO, and screen - and is explicitly not a drawn playbook: it records what was called, not the designed play.
The week-3 edge is the sum of prior times signed signal across the whole table; dark families add zero and the live families are not scaled up to compensate for the dark share.

The model keeps a deliberate dark share of 0.24 of total prior weight: dark-family coefficients stay at zero so those families are named rather than forgotten, and a missing row is never filled with a guess.

On-field efficiency is a shrunk opponent-adjusted blend of 55% pass EPA residual, 15% rush EPA residual, 15% CPOE, 10% explosive-pass rate, and 5% interception luck; the 2025 season is the prior and 2026 weeks 1-2 are the observation.

Signal-family priors split by role: premise families are on_field_efficiency 0.14, scheme_play_design 0.12, availability 0.12, schedule_and_body 0.08, historical_strength 0.08, trench_personnel 0.05, chemistry 0.04, and airwave 0.05; market_context 0.05 is context_not_objective, calibration_meters 0.03 is a meter, and weather_physics 0.07, coaching 0.06, officials 0.04, bio_nutrition 0.04, narrative_contract 0.03, social 0.00 are dark.
Brier, Kelly, and Bradley-Terry are treated as meters - calibration instruments - not as objective signal families in the edge sum.
Officials is dark on the 2025 holdout, including games that have a referee name - a named referee does not reactivate the family.
Airwave enters the edge at a prior of 0.05 as the questionable-and-doubtful skill-player wire; it is explicitly not a second copy of the out list.
New signal candidates pass through selectPart in packages/prediction-engine/src/reasoning/part-selector.ts; the eight families already in the sum are registered in live-edge-registry.ts.
Market price is treated as context (context_not_objective), not as an objective to fit; the price is context.

The edge decomposes into parts as signed signal times family prior: for LAC at BUF, on_field_efficiency signed 1.000 contributes 0.140 points, availability signed 0.667 contributes 0.080 points, and airwave signed -0.208 subtracts 0.010 points.
Calibration fed to the contract for week 3: n=3018, ECE=0.0338, Brier=0.2312 against a baseline of 0.2122, with drift=0.0057.
The GSE score is an action-quality number from 0 to 100, explicitly not a win probability, and publishablePick stayed false for all 16 scored games (publishablePick true count: 0).
Fantasy position weights are set by inverse MAE from 2025 half-PPR: QB 0.1522, RB 0.2496, TE 0.3287, WR 0.2694.
A signal candidate's honesty bar f1 is |r| >= 0.08 and |slope| > standard error on a walk-forward; otherwise the candidate stays dark.
Officials stays dark when a referee is named for week 3 because on the 2025 holdout its slope magnitude 0.01007 was not greater than its standard error 0.01028 - inside one standard error.
Weather_physics stays dark because its wind_mph slope magnitude 0.135 was not greater than its standard error 0.1618, and no week-3 row existed for it.
Coaching stays dark because its fourth-down go-rate grain had |r|=0.014, under the 0.08 honesty threshold.

Trench_personnel's representative is quarterback hits per dropback, validated at 2025 walk-forward r=0.241 with n=250; a tackle-out drag is explicitly not a second trench part, preventing double counting inside the same family.
Scheme_play_design's helper is drive-start, capped at 0.15, and is not the MOVE-37 sin formula - an explicit guard against smuggling an unverified formula into the family.
Availability covers only out-designation players; questionable skill players stay on the airwave family, so the same absence is never counted twice.
Schedule_and_body's rest term only enters if it cleared |slope| > standard error on margin; otherwise the signed rest difference contributes zero.
Chemistry treats the same-quarterback case as a real zero and keeps zero in the sum - a genuine null signal is retained rather than replaced or imputed.
Airwave's representative stays locked; when a game has no numeric airwave value the contribution is zero, and that zero is explicitly not a stored fit.
publishes_pick is false; the trace sees the live parts but its confidence is explicitly not a win probability.

A 2025 prop slope is defined as how a frozen projection regresses toward the actual stat on that season block (yards for the yard props, receptions for receptions); the document states explicitly that slope is not a player edge, not a probability, not +EV, and not a pick.
The 2026 sample never chooses the shrinkage weight w: the 2026 n, MAE, and slope are a watch row only, not a basis for choosing the weight.
Each player row uses the 2025 position-specific slope (by_position), not the prop-level slope, since by_position exists for every mapped position.
Salary only marks who is on the slate and is not printed and not a recommendation; AvgPointsPerGame is ignored because it is not a projection used in the props surface.
Market prices were not on the salary file, so agreement with a posted player prop is impossible from those inputs alone - a book prop is not invented.
Every charted player is a signal; 2269 signals were charted in week 3, 141 to 160 per game, with a median game total of 43.5.

The offensive-line multiplier comes from a 2024-2025 fit, not a guess: a starting tackle who is out is -11.3%, one who did not practice is -7.5%, one who was limited is -5.0%, and a full practice is no change; a backup guard is not in the fit.
An out or did-not-practice starting tackle lowers the team's skill players, while a questionable tag with a full practice does not lower them.
Because no player prop price was on the game file, agreement is defined as opportunity plus the total plus the team edge; a book prop is not invented.

The part-selector scalarizer gates candidate signals on three factors: f1 honesty (|r| >= 0.08 and |slope| > standard error on a walk-forward, else reject), f2 duplication (this direction already has a representative), and f3 a missing week-3 row; the scalarizer uses ideal (0,0,0) with lambda weights (0.5, 0.3, 0.2).
Inventory is not a wire: eight transcribed tables were inventoried, the eight live parts on the week-3 edge were left unchanged, publishes_pick stayed false, and no new prior was set.

ARBY's blend is a shrinkage recipe: last season 0.65, this season 0.35, then split the result with a yards-per-carry term; the model's priors already shrink 2025 toward 2026 weeks 1-2, and the ARBY rank itself is their number and does not enter the edge.

Targets behind the line were recomputed from 2025 pbp (air_yards < 0) on a weeks-4-18 walk-forward, n=224: raw r=-0.116, slope=-1.058, se=0.609, but after residualizing on prior point margin the partial r fell to -0.083 - under 0.08 - so it is stored, not a live helper; manufactured targets are not an independent edge on this sample.

Drive-TD rate (drive_ended_with_score), recomputed on the same walk-forward n=224, had raw r=+0.115, slope=0.596, se=0.345, but correlates 0.676 with prior margin and its partial r after margin flips to -0.138 - the scoring family counted twice - so it stays dark and the pasted 4.0 is not joined.

WR separation as an NGS grain was already measured at r=+0.010 and left unused; the team separation board was rejected anyway because it listed Jaylen Waddle on the Denver Broncos - a dirty board is not joined.
12-personnel EPA/play was rejected because the pbp extract has no offense_personnel column so it cannot be recomputed locally, and EPA/play would be the efficiency family counted twice.
Pass-rush win rate was rejected as a commercial grade with only five teams, while the trench representative is already quarterback hits per dropback (2025 r=0.241); the pasted 67.2 is not joined.
A pasted rank from X is not a row: raw pasted numbers never enter the edge without a local walk-forward recomputation.

Fewer flags per game (Eck 10.9, Allen 11.1, Novak 11.1) means fewer free first downs via DPI/holding — a marginal drag on total plays for DFS — while high-flag crews (Blakeman 13.2, Rogers 13.1, Hochuli 13.0, Hill 13.0) extend drives, especially Hill (No. 1 in DPI/roughing auto-first-downs since 2021).

The WR/TE full-pool method: qualifying filter of Week 1 route participation >50% OR target share >15% (strict); Week 1 usage from RotoWire's 'NFL Box Score Breakdown Week 1' (NFL Next Gen data; YPRR = receiving yards / routes run; table wins over commentary on conflicts); 101 qualifying players across 30 teams; percentiles computed against only the 101-player qualifying pool by mean-rank scoring: (number below + 0.5 x number tied) / valid observations x 100; [ELITE] = 90th+ percentile, [WEAK] = 25th or lower.
equation: percentile = (number below + 0.5 * number tied) / valid observations * 100

claim: YPRR is defined as receiving yards divided by routes run (used in the WR/TE full-pool report).

Salary-sourcing discipline: only The Huddle (published 9/19) and DK Network (9/15, primetime) are allowed salary sources, each surfaced with [2P]; where neither supplies a salary the exact phrase 'not publicly surfaced from allowed sources' is used; ancillary stats appear only where a dated public source exists, otherwise 'not publicly surfaced.'

An IG post by @dugoutforever (2026-06-24) citing a Sean Zerillo / Action Network analysis speculates the MLB baseball may have changed mid-season 2026 and gotten livelier; MLB announced nothing, and the note treats this as an UNVERIFIED lead that must not touch model priors until verified.

Ball liveliness is a totals-model input: if the ball changes mid-season, any totals prior trained on early-season data drifts. The documented wire-up is to verify the Zerillo analysis (check whether the effect survived the 2026 season, i.e. did HR rates regress), and if real, file it as a regime-change covariate (ball-batch era flag) in the context matrix — exactly the 'regime change' problem covered by the v5.3.0 build spec's Workstream 5.

The GSE eval preregistration template (source pattern: @datasciencebrain 2026-09-11, 'Not the pipeline. The measurement.') requires writing the success criterion into code BEFORE running anything and committing it so the goalposts cannot move.

The preregistration template requires: a one-sentence hypothesis; a frozen dataset with train/cutoff and test window (no peeking past the cutoff); a primary metric with a threshold and a sample size fixed in advance; validity gates (no train/test leakage, the baseline is the real incumbent not a strawman, no threshold tuning after seeing the answer, and an exact test used — McNemar / binomial / paired — with p reported); and a kill rule (if the criterion is not met at the preregistered n, the experiment dies — no 'one more tweak').

Results discipline: publish failures anyway — a failing number is proof the threshold was not tuned. The template applies to the TimesFM-3 eval, the prop-prompt pack validation, and any new metric from the benchmark lane.

Constraint: the GSE engine's `picks` table holds SPREAD/MONEYLINE/TOTAL only — no prop market — so the prop prompt pack serves validation/alpha research against public prop lines and GSE content, and never enters the pick path until a prop market exists in the engine.

The anytime-TD prompt template asks an NFL prop analyst to estimate a probability of an anytime touchdown from structured inputs: role data (routes/run, target share, red-zone targets last 4, snaps, goal-line carries), matchup (opp red-zone TD allowed rate, opp DVOA vs position, game total), weather, and relevant inactives — returning JSON with p_anytime_td, fair_odds, edge_vs_line, top_factors and kill_factors. It carries a calibration rule (probabilities must be honest, not confident-sounding: 'a 0.15 with a reason beats a 0.4 with vibes') and a constraint to use ONLY the data provided, never invent stats.

The home-run hitter prompt template mirrors a power/pitcher/park/wind frame: it estimates p_hr from batter power (barrels/PA, hard-hit%, average exit velocity, launch-angle sweet-spot%), pitcher vulnerability (HR/9, FB%, HR allowed to L/RHB splits), park (park HR factor), conditions (wind direction/mph, temperature, humidity), and lineup context (batting order, OBP of hitters ahead).

The preregistered validation protocol requires logging every prompt output plus the public line at kickoff/first pitch (committed, no editing after), writing the success criterion BEFORE the first run (e.g., the TD prompt achieving positive CLV vs closing lines over n=100 graded props — CLV, not win rate), using exact binomial/McNemar tests on the CLV sign, publishing failures anyway, and killing the pack with no post-hoc threshold tuning if no edge shows after the preregistered n.
The pack runs the same prompt across two models — a cheap router for volume and a frontier model for the shortlist — applying the 56%-cheaper local-router pattern referenced from the action board.

Method: the study's sample is all nflverse play-by-play plays 2013–2023 where passer_player_name == 'C.Keenum' and receiver_player_name is non-null (a targeted attempt; throwaways/spikes and sacks excluded), n=2,270 targets across HOU, LA, MIN, DEN, WAS, CLE, BUF; receiver positions joined from that season's nflverse roster via GSIS id (zero unknown positions); the league baseline is the same filter for all QBs, n=203,055 targets.

Keenum's career target split is WR 59.6% / TE 20.4% / RB-FB 20.0% versus the 2013–23 league average of 59.3% / 20.9% / 19.7% — essentially league-average with no career-long positional favoritism; he is not a 'TE guy' or a 'checkdown guy' relative to the league, and his distribution follows his team's personnel and scheme.

Keenum's career most-targeted receiver is Adam Thielen (MIN 2017): 145 targets, 88 receptions, 1,201 yards; followed by Stefon Diggs (MIN 2017, 106 targets) and Tavon Austin (LA 2015–16, 104 targets).

The layoff-return set is 10 games with >=10 targeted attempts after a gap of >=8 weeks since Keenum's previous game with any target, totaling n=323 targets — e.g., 2014-12-21 BAL @ HOU (41 attempts, 53.0-week gap), 2019-09-08 WAS @ PHI (43 attempts, 36.0-week gap), 2023-12-17 HOU @ TEN (34 attempts, 62.0-week gap).

In the return set the positional split is WR 62.2% / TE 20.1% / RB-FB 17.6% versus his career 59.6% / 20.4% / 20.0% — when rusty, Keenum is slightly MORE WR-heavy and LESS RB-heavy than his career baseline; he does not lean harder on TEs or RB checkdowns at the position level.

The 'safety blanket' shows up at the individual-player level, not the position level: 2019-09-08 WAS @ PHI, Chris Thompson (RB) took 10 targets (23% of all targets) with RB checkdown share spiking to 30.2% vs 20% career — the one clear outlier in the study; 2021-10-21 DEN @ CLE, slot receiver Jarvis Landry took 8 targets (25%); 2023-12-17 HOU @ TEN, Noah Brown took 11 targets (32% share); 2022-01-09 CIN @ CLE, Landry took 8 of 24 (33%).

The study's blanket pattern (flagged as general football knowledge, not present in nflverse pbp): the blanket is whoever owns the most separation-friendly role in that specific offense — slot receiver, receiving RB, or WR1 — not a fixed position for Keenum (Landry was a career slot receiver, Thompson was Washington's dedicated receiving/third-down RB, Brown played primarily X/Z outside for Houston).

Study caveats: the return set is only 323 targets across 10 games and each individual rusty start is one game (32–43 targets), so single-game variance dominates and the pattern is suggestive, not predictive; team/scheme confounds are large (the blanket follows the roster — Gruden's WAS, Stefanski's CLE, Ryans/Slowik's HOU — not Keenum himself); no alignment (slot/X/Y) data exists in nflverse pbp; and Keenum had not played since 2023-12-24 and was 38, with the 2026 Bears' Ben Johnson scheme having no Keenum history to draw on.
