Cost baseline for the Brev/NVIDIA skills stack: NVIDIA Build hosted endpoints (integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1, OpenAI-compatible) offer a free developer tier with no credit card, community-reported at ~40 RPM per key per model (traffic-dependent; exact quota UNVERIFIED); the tier is explicitly dev/eval only — production user traffic needs NVIDIA AI Enterprise. Every skill in the catalog is Apache-2.0/CC-BY open source (github.com/NVIDIA/skills and blueprint repos), so the burn is always the Brev box: Brev bills per-hour per instance, per-GPU-hour rates are unpublished (UNVERIFIED), and the standing discipline is spin up, run the batch job, tear down.

NV-Tesseract forecasting (tao-finetune-nv-tesseract-forecasting) is transformer-based multivariate time-series forecasting on a MOMENT-1-large backbone with self-supervised pretraining, Apache-2.0 with weights public on Hugging Face (no auth); it has three inference modes — standard, DARR (context-enhanced kNN retrieval blending against similar historical windows), and interpretability (lag×horizon attribution, trajectory stability, PDF report). Fine-tuning freezes the encoder and trains only the forecasting head (5 epochs, batch 8, lr 1e-4 defaults), runs on 1× CPU minimum with 1× GPU of >=8GB VRAM recommended; unlike the non-commercial-licensed TimesFM-3 (research-only), the Apache-2.0 license means it can live in a production forecasting path.

Earth2Studio is NVIDIA's open-source AI weather/climate framework (Apache-2.0; models and data open): the data-fetch skill downloads weather/climate data for specific variables, times and lead times from public sources like GFS/ERA5, and the deterministic-forecast skill builds single-member forecast scripts (e.g., FourCastNet3 + GFS() data + ZarrBackend in ~10 lines); data-fetch is CPU + network while inference-class models run on a single modest GPU.

cuDF provides pandas-compatible GPU DataFrames with a zero-code-change cudf.pandas accelerator mode (set an env var) plus dask-cuDF for multi-GPU scaling, fast Parquet I/O, joins and groupbys; requirements are Volta+ (compute capability >=7.0), CUDA 11.2+/12+, Python 3.10+, Linux only. The dossier cites 10–50× speedups on pandas-slow groupbys for backtest-ledger crunching (3,411+ picks, per-season CV splits) and tick-level odds-API line-movement ETL.

NeMo Retriever 26.8.1 is a single `retriever` CLI that runs extract → embed → LanceDB vector index over folders of PDFs, images, Office files, HTML, text, audio and video; extraction stages are layout/page-elements, OCR, table/structure extraction, chart detection and VLM captioning, embedding via nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2 with optional rerank. It is CPU-host viable when NVIDIA_API_KEY routes the heavy stages to hosted endpoints, so ingest is a one-shot job and querying a LanceDB table is CPU-trivial.

The NVIDIA RAG Blueprint is a production RAG stack: NV-Ingest document ingestion, Elasticsearch (default since 2.6.0; Milvus optional), SeaweedFS object store, NeMo Guardrails, Agentic RAG (plan-and-execute pipelines, 2.6.0), UI, MCP server and an OpenAI-compatible search endpoint. Two cost tiers exist — CPU-light (hosted endpoints, no GPU) and full self-host (default LLM now nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b with reasoning on; 2×H100/4×A100 reference for 70B-class; 2.5.0 added RTX 6000 MIG support); the batch pattern is index on GPU, serve retrieval from CPU, shut the GPU down. Known limitation: B200 unsupported for image captioning/guardrails/VLM inference/Nemotron Parse.

rag-eval is the RAG Blueprint quality benchmark: feed it corpus/ + train.json, it runs evaluate_rag.py, toggles retrieval/generation flags (reranker on/off, query rewriting, temperature), and reports RAGAS metrics (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall) as JSON with failure triage. The evaluator itself is CPU-light; the RAGAS judge calls need NVIDIA_API_KEY (free tier).

NeMo Data Designer is a declarative synthetic-data pipeline builder (YAML or Python config): columns/types/prompts/validators resolved as a dependency DAG, batched, validated and judged, orchestrating external LLM inference servers (NIM, OpenAI, vLLM) over HTTP; it ships SFT chat, tool-calling and DPO preference-pair templates with preview-then-scale-to-10k+ workflows, and requires no GPU itself (the endpoint holds it). Standing caveat: synthetic data is for content/eval, never train a pick engine on synthetic game outcomes.

nemotron-customize chains repo-native Nemotron customization pipelines via a `nemotron step` CLI: curation (nemo_curator JSONL cleaning), translation, SFT/PEFT (AutoModel or Megatron-Bridge), CPT/pretraining, RL alignment (DPO/RLVR/GRPO/RLHF), BYOB/MCQ benchmarks, checkpoint conversion (Megatron→HF) and ModelOpt quantization/pruning/distillation; it is Apache-2.0 and commercial-ready, with local GPU, Slurm or Lepton (metered, UNVERIFIED pricing) backends — LoRA/PEFT on an 8B-class model fits a single 24GB+ card while full SFT/RLHF wants multi-GPU.

The Video Search and Summarization (VSS) Blueprint is NVIDIA's GA Metropolis blueprint for video-analytics AI agents: ingest massive volumes of live or archived video and extract insights via natural-language video search (fusion search across video embeddings + CV attribute embeddings — Cosmos Embed1 + CV attributes), video summarization (LVS/VLM, up to 100× faster than manual review per NVIDIA), interactive visual Q&A, real-time alerts with VLM verification, object tracking, event review, audio transcription and multimodal fusion. Deployment profiles include base, lvs, alerts, search, edge, brev, ngc and prerequisites; the 'complete remote' topology needs only an 8GB-VRAM host with VLM/LLM/embedding/reranker all remote, while the default local topology is 8× A100-80GB/H100/H200/B200 or 8× L40S.

The VSS Brev launchable provisions 2× RTX PRO 6000 (AWS) or 8× L40S (Crusoe); RTX PRO 6000 is a 96GB Blackwell card retailing ~$16,000 (Aug 2026) — instance hours on that class are not cheap, hence the cap discipline.

vss-ask-video asks the VSS agent's video_understanding tool a fresh visual question about a recorded clip ('what coverage is the safety in?', 'is the route cut off?') and returns a VLM answer grounded in the actual pixels — questions that cannot be answered from metadata or prior tool output. The lane documents a real doc bug: the skill catalog describes it as calling the agent's /generate endpoint, but the actual SKILL.md hard-rules 'never call /generate' and posts directly to the VLM's chat/completions endpoint, with NVIDIA's docs repo being corrected (Sep 2026).

DeepStream 9.x development via the Python pyservicemaker API covers video-analytics pipelines, GStreamer processing, TensorRT inference integration, object detection/tracking and Kafka output; YOLO-class detectors with NvDCF/NvSORT trackers run in real time on T4/L4/A10-class GPUs, TensorRT engines build once per GPU architecture, and the SDK plus containers are free on NGC (free account/API key).

deepstream-import-vision-model performs fully autonomous object-detection model bring-up: give it a HuggingFace or NGC URL and it acquires the model (downloads ONNX or exports SafeTensors→ONNX via optimum-cli, extracts labels), builds a dynamic TensorRT engine via trtexec with batch-size scaling and warm-cache reuse, generates a custom nvinfer bbox parser and .so, runs single-stream KITTI validation then a multi-stream sweep, and emits 5 benchmark charts plus a Markdown/HTML/PDF report. Scope is object-detection models only (DETR/RT-DETR, YOLO family, GroundingDINO/OWL-ViT zero-shot); classification/segmentation/pose are rejected up front.

Nemotron Speech (the public name for what docs still call Riva) is a single routing surface for ASR, TTS and translation (NMT): cloud-hosted inference via build.nvidia.com free endpoints, self-hosted Docker deployment, gRPC/HTTP/WebSocket ASR clients, custom NeMo model builds via riva-build, and pipeline tuning (Silero VAD, Sortformer diarization, chunk size, pronunciation/SSML for TTS). Self-hosted ASR NIMs (Parakeet, Canary) run on 8–16GB-VRAM-class GPUs, but self-hosted Riva NIMs gate on an NVIDIA AI Enterprise entitlement (the paid tier). Companion skill nemotron-asr-finetune routes domain/language adaptation through the cheapest sufficient path.

The digital-health clinical-asr setup/build/eval/finetune skills define a domain-agnostic ASR flywheel: term curation → synthetic benchmark generation → keyword-error-rate (KER) scoring → fine-tuning of NVIDIA Parakeet TDT v2 (NeMo SFT recipe, nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2, bf16-mixed, lr 3e-4, fits 16 GB VRAM at batch_size 4). The models are CC-BY-4.0 (commercial-safe); nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization pairs with a multitalker Parakeet for speaker-attributed transcripts; batched transcription of Parakeet-TDT-0.6b-v2 runs at ~3400× real-time.

Nemotron Parse (arXiv:2511.20478) is an end-to-end vision-language model that extracts formatted text (Markdown/LaTeX), bounding boxes and semantic block classes from PDFs with reading order preserved; a token-compressed (TC) variant keeps accuracy with much lower latency for batch/edge. Nemotron Parse 2.0 (Hugging Face, Aug 2026, <1B params, vision-encoder-decoder) converts scanned PDFs/slides/forms/charts into structured text including chart-to-table parsing. It is the extraction engine behind nv-ingest, which is the ingestion microservice consumed by the RAG Blueprint.

Cosmos Dataset Search (official NVIDIA blueprint) is a vector-search workflow over video archives: ingest video collections, generate embeddings with the Cosmos-embed NIM, store them in Milvus (cuVS-accelerated), and serve text-to-video and video-to-video search through a React UI + REST API + CLI. Built for AV scenario mining, the mechanics are pure semantic video retrieval.

cuOpt is NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated decision-optimization engine with Python, C, gRPC and REST server APIs, supporting vehicle routing (TSP/VRP/PDP), linear/quadratic programming and mixed-integer programming (beta); the NVIDIA skills catalog exposes it as six skills (cuopt-install, cuopt-multi-objective-exploration, cuopt-numerical-optimization-api, cuopt-numerical-optimization-formulation, cuopt-routing-api-python, cuopt-server-api-python), installable via `npx skills add nvidia/skills --skill cuopt-numerical-optimization-api --yes`. cuOpt itself is open-source (cost is the Brev box only), runs on modest GPUs, and its server API allows hosting it as a service. The dossier frames DFS lineup construction as exactly a MILP — maximize projected points subject to salary cap, position slots, exposure caps and stack constraints — that cuOpt MILP can replace OR-Tools CP-SAT on deterministically and auditable, with multi-objective-exploration mapping the ceiling-vs-floor-vs-ownership tradeoff surface.

cufolio is GPU-accelerated Mean-CVaR / Mean-Variance portfolio optimization via the cuOpt solver (Apache-2.0): KDE scenario generation, efficient frontier, walk-forward backtest against benchmarks, scheduled/drift-trigger rebalancing, from price data (S&P 500/100, Dow 30) or user CSV. It is equities, not sports — but the dossier proposes stealing the machinery: scenario generation + walk-forward backtest + rebalancing ports to bankroll/Kelly staking optimization by treating the pick ledger as a return series and optimizing stake sizing under downside-CVaR constraints, backtested against flat-staking.

The AI-Q Blueprint is NVIDIA's deep-research agent platform: intent classification → clarification → multi-source retrieval via MCP servers → synthesis with Nemotron reasoning models → cited report. aiq-deploy stands it up (Docker Engine + Compose v2 default: AI-Q backend + PostgreSQL, browser UI on :3000; also uv-based Python CLI or Helm/K8s modes) and aiq-research submits research jobs to a running backend and polls/retrieves the cited reports. The backend runs CPU-only if the LLM points at hosted NVIDIA endpoints; self-hosting Llama 3.3 70B Instruct per the nim-deploy reference wants 2× H100 NVL or 4× A100. Web research needs a search-provider key (Tavily has a free tier; exact quota UNVERIFIED).

NVIDIA Dynamo (github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo, open source, launched GTC 2025) is a cluster-level LLM inference orchestrator wrapping vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM with an OpenAI-compatible Rust frontend, a router (round-robin, KV-cache-aware, least-loaded, device-aware-weighted, direct, random) and worker pools; dynamo-router-starter configures the frontend router and runs a smoke test (scripts/check_router_health.py hits /v1/models + one chat completion). It runs on a single GPU — community deployments serve 8B-class models on 1× L40S (48GB) — with KV-aware routing as pure software (including an approximate mode); real prefill/decode disaggregation needs 2+ GPUs.

NemoClaw (github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw, Apache-2.0) is NVIDIA's open-source reference stack for running always-on AI agents more safely: guided onboarding, routed inference, deny-by-default network policy (policy.yaml declares every allowed host/port/verb/binary — anything else gets a proxy 403), and lifecycle management through a single CLI, with agents running inside OpenShell sandboxes (filesystem + network + process isolation, capability drops). Three first-class agents are supported: OpenClaw, Hermes and LangChain Deep Agents Code. It is the one lane-1 skill with a genuine one-click Brev launchable (reference sizing 8 vCPU / 16 GB RAM / 80 GB disk, no GPU — inference is a remote endpoint). The dossier flags a NAME COLLISION: NVIDIA's 'Hermes' is Hermes Agent (get-hermes.ai), a third-party coding harness, and is NOT Garrett's Hermes (the overnight builder on the Minis phone app).

nemo-rl-session-memory is an agent workflow playbook, not a server: keep a durable, human-readable session record in a repo-local session/<timestamp>/ directory with four files — session_state.md (goal, subtask, plan, blockers, next actions), timeline.md (append-only action log), files.md (what was inspected/changed and why), handoff.md (resume instructions for the next agent). Checkpoint periodically and resume by reading the latest three files. Zero GPU, $0; it installs into the agent's skills directory and travels wherever the coding agent runs.

The TileGym/cuTile DGX Spark playbook (supplied by Garrett 2026-09-25; verdict: parked): benchmarks and integrates high-performance GPU kernels written with the cuTile Python DSL, compiling to Tile IR and JIT-targeting DGX Spark (sm_121) and B300 (sm_103); kernel coverage is FMHA, MLA/MLA-decoding, MatMul/BMM/Group GEMM, RMSNorm, RoPE, SiLU/SwiGLU, Softmax, Dropout; pinned v1.3.0, CUDA 13.2.0, Nsight 2025.1.3. The verdict is infrastructure optimization with no current lane fit — parked with a clear trigger condition: revisit only after profiling proves local inference cost or latency is a measured bottleneck.

The lane-4 catalog sweep's honest no-fit verdicts on five mapping targets: nothing in the NVIDIA/Brev engineering catalog fits lead generation/outreach/prospecting, social content pipelines (scheduling/drafting/analytics), website building, SEO, or marketplace/ecommerce — the catalog covers physical AI, CUDA-X, inference and optimization; and no sports-specific analytics/prediction/odds skill exists — Earth2Studio (weather) is the only modeling-adjacent item, with the real sports-relevant finds being infrastructure (cuOpt, Cosmos, ASR, Tesseract). Separately, the quantum route (cudaq-guide) was assessed and rejected as premature: QUBO/TSP encodings blow up (n² qubits for TSP), hardware access is expensive and experimental, and cuOpt's classical MILP dominates on every practical axis today.

The sweep notes adjacent-but-out-of-scope community resources: the opencue/skills repo (not NVIDIA) has marketing/ (content, social, campaigns) and medusa/ (Medusa v2 ecommerce) categories — outside the NVIDIA catalog, unverified. Also dismissed: skill-card-generator (governance docs only), physical-ai-video-data-augmentation / physical-ai-defect-image-generation (synthetic training-data generation — flagged under the hard video rule), dali-dynamic-mode (GPU data-loading utility, not a capability), nemo-automodel-*/mcore-linting (already shortlisted or pure training plumbing), omniverse-*/physicsnemo-discover (simulation/engineering twins, no lane fit).

Missed skills from the same VSS/DeepStream repos worth flagging: vss-search-archive (natural-language search over video archives via multi-embedding fusion — Cosmos-Embed1 — + CV attribute matching + VLM critique; ingests files/RTSP), vss-manage-video-io-storage (VIOS REST: recording timelines, clip extraction, snapshot capture, sensor/stream management), vss-deploy-detection-tracking-2d (prebuilt 2D detection+tracking microservice via REST), vss-generate-video-report (formatted markdown analysis reports per clip or incident range), vss-manage-alerts (real-time alert rules on streams with VLM verification), and nemotron-asr-finetune (cheapest-path ASR domain/language adaptation).

The brief's evidence-grade key: VERIFIED (observed directly in a cited primary/secondary source that session), ATTRIBUTED (stated by a named source, not independently audited), ESTIMATED (third-party estimate, directional only), UNVERIFIABLE (guru claim with no auditable basis), DISPUTED (sources disagree) — a methodology for grading every content-strategy claim.

Content ID claims (automated match; the NFL can monetize, block, or track the video — no channel strike, fair use not evaluated at claim stage) are distinct from copyright strikes (formal DMCA takedowns; three strikes within 90 days terminates the channel), and a rejected dispute can escalate a claim into a strike — practitioner shorthand: 'claims are a tax; strikes are a death sentence.'

A USC law-journal paper documented the NFL demanding removal of 3,000+ YouTube game clips in 2006, and in 2007 the NFL objected to even 20 seconds of game footage in a law professor's copyright-warning video — evidence that no safe 'under X seconds' rule exists and the NFL has been the strictest rights-holder since YouTube's earliest days.

YouTube's monetization rules are a separate wall from copyright: sports highlight compilations with minimal commentary are explicitly named as 'reused content' that can be denied monetization, and the July 2025 policy update renamed 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content,' aimed at template-following mass-produced uploads.

Tim Jenkins (All Things QB) applied for the NFL's Access Pass, was rejected, and continued using footage anyway — described as a tightrope where the NFL can claim or strike at any time; enforcement is uneven, not predictable, and 'too small to get caught' is luck, not a strategy.

The Center for Media & Social Impact's Code of Best Practices in Fair Use for Online Video, Principle TWO ('Using copyrighted material for illustration or example'): illustrative quotation is fair use when it is important to the larger purpose but subordinate to it, harnesses the material for a new purpose creating new value; limitations include drawing from a range of sources, keeping each quotation no longer than necessary, and attributing — guidance, not a safe harbor.

National Basketball Association v. Motorola, Inc. (105 F.3d 841, 2d Cir. 1997): facts are not copyrightable — Motorola and STATS did not infringe by reproducing only facts from NBA broadcasts rather than the expression — so independently writing posts from scores, down/distance, formations, play outcomes, and statistics is lawful, though a reporter's phrasing, graphic design, database, or footage is not free.

The U.S. Copyright Office states 'there is no formula to ensure that a predetermined percentage or amount of a work — or specific number of words, lines, pages, copies — may be used without permission,' and even a small amount can weigh against fair use if it is the 'heart' of the work (Harper & Row v. Nation) — so the '1–2 sentence quote is automatically safe' idea is false.

PFF's terms (updated 2026-09-04) are unusually explicit: §1.9 permits sharing, quoting, or screenshotting individual PFF grades, statistics, or excerpts of free articles on personal noncommercial social accounts with attribution/linking and without bulk substitution; §1.10 permits monetized creator content to reference/quote/display individual items of Free Content with credit, links, no bulk/database-like use, and no implied PFF endorsement.

Per the Library of Congress, published U.S. works registered for copyright through Dec 31, 1963 are in the public domain only unless the copyright was renewed — and renewal status requires a per-item copyright search (Copyright Office records, Stanford renewal database); archive.org hosting alone proves nothing, and the NFL has affirmatively claimed copyright over historic footage such as Super Bowl I.

Adoptable kernels: payoff-on-last-slide carousel structure, comment-gated DM funnel, kickoff-countdown urgency posts, hiding like counts while a record is being built, daily cadence discipline. Explicitly do NOT copy: 'rigged' framing, vibes-only records, post-hoc prediction posting.

AWS SageMaker football-tracking blog: transfer learning with YOLOv3 vs Faster-RCNN vs SSD on football detection; honest accounting — no per-architecture or per-stratum numbers exist in the text; the 'Faster-RCNN best on small objects (the football); SSD underperforms on small objects' finding is qualitative. HPO: 100 jobs (Bayesian + random), lr continuous in [0.001, 0.1], backbones resnet50_v1b/resnet101_v1d, objective = highest mAP on held-out test. The real kernel: a 5-axis error-stratification protocol (occlusion high/low, box size small/large, aspect tall/wide, camera endzone/sideline, contrast high/low) whose output is a per-stratum mAP table used to direct strategic data collection — not just to pick the model.

Harsh Raj LinkedIn post 'Tracking American Football Players with Computer Vision' (2026, all 10 claims verified against visible text): ~30 semi-supervised Roboflow frames -> RF-DETR segmentation as per-frame seer -> SAM 2 with adapted memory bank for pile-ups -> OpenCV classical geometry to cancel camera motion (no learning) -> small OCR pass on sharp crops for long-gap reappearances (jersey digits). Key insight: appearance ReID is a dead end in identical uniforms — identity comes from motion continuity instead ('You can't confuse two identical twins if you never took your eyes off one of them'); a player buried in a pile never left the frame, so follow his pixels through it instead of re-recognizing after. Stated limitation: opening frames (worst camera motion) are future work; no code and no numeric metrics in the post.

Chung Brown thesis (May 2024, 30 pages): semi-automated labeled-formation pipeline from Notre Dame 2021-22 home broadcast games — YOLOv3 detection + yard-line detection via Hough transform + hash-mark detection (LoG blobs + Hough) + yard-line labeling; preprocessing order: score-bug removal FIRST (bug text would inject false Hough votes), then field-boundary detection. Formation images + play-by-play -> run/pass: logistic regression 59.7%, VGG-16 on images 66.67%, VGG-16 + play-by-play 68.89% (10-fold CV, n=450, 52% run base rate). Yard-line labeling FAILED both attempts: numeral template matching failed under broadcast rotation/scale, and LOS anchoring via highest y-gradient failed due to noise. Honest parameter accounting: the thesis contains ZERO numeric parameters (verified by full-text search) — every derived value needs a first tuning run on real footage.

Chung's hash-mark line detection (the key technical contribution): direct Hough fails on hash marks because the marks are short segments separated by gaps (Hough accumulator's collinear-point count is noise-dominated) and white-jerseyed players near the marks skew the fit. Fix: Laplacian-of-Gaussian (LoG) blob detection first (LoG responds strongly to compact bright/dark regions at the scale of the Gaussian sigma), keep only small-radius blobs (rejects players and yard lines), then Hough over the filtered blobs with horizontal angle filtering. Yard-line ∩ hash-mark-line intersections are then true 2D correspondences (non-colinear by construction) suitable for homography.

Sloan 2018 Paper #5571 (Ajmeri & Shah, MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference, All-22 film at 5 fps): standardization pipeline Hough lines -> rotation correction via arccos using LOS + perpendicular companion line -> LOS detection via O-line proximity; per-screenshot yard calibration from 5-yard line spacing; frame-1 reference-point drift correction (highest point of a full white line in frame 1 cancels camera-follow drift); speed = euclidean distance / frame-rate -> yards -> mph; full game (~50 offensive plays) labeled in <5 min. Formation classification from pre-snap coordinates relative to QB: CART 86.5% QB position (Shotgun/Under Center/Pistol) and 72.3% formation across 29 classes (Naive Bayes/SVM/kNN/logreg worse).

Sloan 2018 worked speed example (DeSean Jackson top speed): 215.5 distance-units over 0.2 s (5 fps), x (1 yard / ~82 units) = 12.8 yd/s, then 12.8 yd/s x 3 ft/yd = 38.4 ft/s, /5280 ft/mi x 3600 s/hr = 26.2 mph. The authors note this reads high vs. Next Gen Stats and recommend relative comparison only (Jackson 22.4 vs Harris 19.3 mph in first 0.6s; Garcon 1.3 fewer yards than Jackson on mirrored comebacks — break-angle precision as a measurable trait). Author-stated limitation: jersey-color tracking breaks under shadows/sunlight RGB variance.

MDPI Electronics 2023, 12(3), 726 ('Automated Pre-Play Analysis of American Football Formations Using Deep Learning', CC BY 4.0, full text read): YOLOv3 single-class player detector with operating point 0.35 chosen by sweeping confidence 0.05 to 0.95 and maximizing F1; ResNet-152 per-player labeling using a green/yellow dot input representation (player of interest = yellow dot) with centroid normalization; 12->8 position label grouping (Center+OG+OT->Offensive Line; CB+Safety->Defensive Back; DE+DT->Defensive Line; QB/RB/TE/WR/LB kept); 25 formations (5 families x 5). Kept augmentations: yard-line affine ('affine suffices because the change in distance between the players is relatively small'), random player shifts, +-2 degree formation rotation; REJECTED player-count modification (accuracy decreased — some formations differ by only 1-2 players, and football always has exactly 11 per side). QB rule (enforce exactly one QB pre-snap) measured +4 percentage points on formation accuracy. Results: 90.3%/98.8%/99.2% module-wise, 84.8% end-to-end — the entire drop from 99.5% on ground-truth inputs is attributed to Module 1 missing occluded players: localization is the bottleneck, not classification.

MDPI Electronics detection-scoring protocol (§5.1): match each ground-truth visible player to the nearest detection; if box-center distance < 20 px -> valid detection; leftover detections -> false positives/duplicates. Reported: 90.3% overall detection accuracy, 94.1% on key offensive players (QB/RB/WR), 88.1% on key defensive players (DBs) — offense is easier than defense. Occluded players were labeled as single-coordinate points (follow-up work: a single bounding box no larger than 5 pixels wide), never guessed full boxes. Dataset: 1,000 images from Madden NFL 2020 PC game, splits 700/300 and 300/200 split by game to maximize variability; 'available on request' only (EA rights).

Mendez 'Image Registration in Sports Analytics' NFL field-mapping tutorial (StatsBomb CV practitioner, full post read): canonical field template 120 x 53.3 px (1 px = 1 yard), hand-drawn elements (sidelines, end lines, end zones, hash marks at true NFL lateral offset — NFL 18 ft 6 in from each sideline vs college 40 ft apart); OpenCV findHomography with 4-point minimum; direction discipline — the post computes template->image (for warpPerspective overlay), but measurement needs image->template (the inverse); colinearity guard: homography.empty() -> refuse with 'Be sure they are not colinear', i.e., never emit a matrix from degenerate correspondences.

Mendez tutorial (continued): the DLT colinearity math (standard derivation): if all correspondences lie on one line, the DLT design matrix rows span a subspace of dimension < 8, the nullspace of A has dimension >= 2, and the condition number kappa(A^T A) = lambda_max / lambda_min -> infinity. Near-colinear is the dangerous case: lambda_min small but nonzero, the solver returns a matrix with fine reprojection error on fitting points while extrapolation meters away explodes — so the guard must measure geometric spread before solving. Generalized guard: >=4 points, 2x2 covariance eigenvalue ratio l2/l1 >= 1e-3 on both src and dst point sets, absolute spread floors, convex-hull area backstop, throwing a named DegenerateCorrespondencesError (colinear-src | colinear-dst | insufficient-spread | too-few) instead of emitting garbage.

Geeklocker Substack 'The Math Behind the NFL's Decision to Call First Downs with Computer Vision' (full 206 lines): accuracy ladder — GNSS ~12' max accuracy at 10-18 Hz, LPS/UWB ~4' max at 10-20 Hz, computer vision ~0.1' at up to 300+ fps (highly camera-dependent), NFL Zebra RFID ball tracking +-6' (2024, per NFL), Wimbledon Hawk-Eye +-0.10' mean error (2020), MLB ball/strike +-0.25' average (2020), FIFA semi-automated offside est. +-1.6'. NFL deployment: Sony Hawk-Eye, six 8K cameras per stadium in a high-elevation ring; the author's arithmetic: each camera covers <= 75 yards = 2,700 inches per camera frame; 8K = 7,680 horizontal pixels; 2,700 / 7,680 = ~0.35 inches per pixel theoretical floor, consistent with the NFL's 'half an inch' expectation told to ESPN. 8K cameras cost >$8,000 each — cost-vs-accuracy tradeoff.

Geeklocker honest-limit distinctions: the NFL is deploying Hawk-Eye ONLY for line-to-gain measurements on a static ball with clear multi-camera view — NOT ball spotting; the chain gang stays as backup. Sloan rotation-deskew reconstruction (the paper gives only the phrase 'arccos(x)' using the LOS and its perpendicular companion line; operands marked [RECONSTRUCTED]): let v_axis be the unit direction vector of the detected field-axis line (the companion perpendicular to the LOS); canonical field long axis e_x = (1, 0); camera roll angle phi = arccos(v_axis . e_x), sign from the cross product (v_axis x e_x)_z; deskew by rotating the image by -phi about its center. Rationale: a single detected line's angle is noisy (Hough quantization + line-fit skew); the perpendicular pair lets you average two independent angle estimates. Honest limitation: rotation-only correction, not perspective — valid as a preconditioner for broadcast side views where the camera is roughly level; the full projective correction is still the DLT's job.

Sloan per-screenshot yard calibration: yard lines are painted every 5 yards; detect adjacent full-field lines, measure pixel separation d_5yd, then px_per_yard = d_5yd / 5, recomputed per frame. GSE use: after fitHomographyDLT returns H, extract the local scale at the image center (||d(xM,yM)/d(xPx,yPx)|| -> meters per pixel -> px per yard via 0.9144) and assert agreement with the independently measured px_per_yard within tolerance (start 10% [DERIVED]); a homography whose scale disagrees with line-spacing measurement is geometrically inconsistent — reject it. This catches bad fits that pass reprojection on their (possibly mislabeled) fitting points.

Tracklet association on real footage (buildTracklets, IoU 0.3, maxGap 5): ~6 concurrent players produce 52-65 tracklets; median tracklet life 0.6-0.8s; up to 40 of 65 tracklets are <=3 frames. The pipeline's camera-motion compensation exists but buildTracklets doesn't use it; motion-aware association (predict + compensate, or higher fps) is the fix. Usable today for counts/heatmaps; not yet for per-player tracking. Tests: 48/48 green under real vitest.

The total-signal wiring spec defines the GSE engine doctrine: ingest every signal possible (on-field, off-field, nutrition, psychology, cognitive, anything that can move a number) and produce the most intelligent reasoning and decisions for fantasy, predictions, props, and parlays; the spec states the engine is explicitly not built to beat the books (that never happens).

Every adjustment rule in the total-signal spec follows the shape TRIGGER → AFFECTED → DIRECTION → MAGNITUDE → LOG, where magnitudes are backtest calibration tasks rather than constants — the spec fixes the shape and backtests fix the numbers.

The offensive-line injury rule: when a starting left tackle or center is ruled out/doubtful and a backup starts, QB passing efficiency drops slightly, RB yards-before-contact drop, checkdown/target share to RB rises slightly as a pressure outlet, and team pass rate drops a tick, with the lineman, replacement, and snap counts logged.

The defensive-secondary injury rule: when a starting safety or CB1/CB2 is out, the opposing QB's pass yards/TD and opposing WR1/WR2/TE projections rise, that defense's projection falls, and the opposing offense's implied total rises slightly, with the replacement's coverage responsibility logged.
The game-script rule: large spreads and high/low totals raise trailing-team pass volume and leading-team run rate, but with a garbage-time discount — 4th-quarter trailing volume is not a role change.
The weather rule: sustained wind thresholds, precipitation, and extreme cold lower pass yards/attempts, affect kick distance, and raise run rate.

The spec's verified state (2026-09-27 repo audit): game_signals held 5,142 rows while the player-level signals table held 0 rows, no adjustment layer existed (zero injury→projection logic), and the optimizer on origin/main was a real exact branch-and-bound with k-best, diverse pools, late swap, correlation GPP layer, exposure control, and payout sim vs a simulated field — all real, no mocks.

The spec's build order: (1) lock the projection source (Garrett's call), (2) register the live DFS slate provider to kill the sample-slate fallback, (3) build adjustment layer v1 (injuries + depth chart), (4) fill the player signals table, (5) off-field intake lane, (6) backtest every rule before it touches a live projection.
Standing rule from the spec: every signal maps to an explicit, logged projection adjustment — no vibes, no unwritten rules — and if Garrett has to explain a rule twice, it was not in the spec.

The GPL explainer's core distinction: MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD mean "do whatever you want, keep the copyright notice" — MIT code can live inside a closed commercial product with no source-sharing; GPL means "do whatever you want, but if you ship a modified version or a product containing it, you ship your source too" (copyleft).

AGPL §13 closes the SaaS loophole: if users interact with the software over a network, the source of the combined work must be offered to them — so running AGPL code server-side to generate anything users see triggers share-back, which is why PanopticPigskin (AGPL-3.0) got a method-only, full-stop verdict for the web product.

LGPL is the linking exception: an unmodified LGPL library may be used in a closed product via dynamic linking or npm dependency without copylefting the host, but copying src/ files into the monorepo or fork-and-vendoring a modified copy creates a derivative work that must be shared under LGPL.

The clean-room path for the coding agent: (1) read the method, (2) close the repo, (3) write a design doc in your own words — inputs, outputs, algorithm stages, (4) implement from the doc never with the source open side-by-side, (5) do not mirror file/function/stage structure or copy names, (6) note provenance in the header: source, license, "independently implemented".

Facts are free, expression is not: numbers, ranks, player IDs, and output schemas-as-facts are safe to use; code structure, comments, pipeline staging, and creative text are not — grounded in Feist v. Rural (1991), which holds facts are not copyrightable expression.

The dataset question: a GPL on a dataset binds the compilation (the curated collection as an expressive work), not the individual facts inside it — reading ECR ranks out of dynastyprocess/data CSVs into our own schema is not creating a derivative work; what is barred is committing their CSV/parquet files into the repo, redistributing them verbatim, or copying the GPL workflows that generate them; the upstream source's ToS (FantasyPros) is a separate question from the repo license.

If GPL code is caught early in a product: remove it and rewrite clean-room before it ships or spreads — GPL-3.0 carries a formal 30-day cure provision for first-time violators; caught late, the holder can demand compliance or sue; the GSE-specific product risk is that an AGPL contamination event forcing source publication of engine code would destroy the moat.

License verification method: each item's license was verified by reading the actual LICENSE file via the GitHub API — dynastyprocess/data GPL-3.0, nflverse/nflverse-pfr GPL-3.0, sumedhk0/PanopticPigskin AGPL-3.0, nflverse/nflverse-pbp CC-BY-4.0, nflverse/nflverse-data CC-BY-4.0, mkreiser/ESPN-Fantasy-Football-API LGPL-3.0-only (npm espn-fantasy-football-api@2.0.1).

dynastyprocess/data verdict: DATA — safely extract facts (player ECR ranks, ADP, projections, player-ID mappings, dynasty values) into our own tables/schema; do NOT commit the CSV/parquet/RDS files into the Sports repo, do NOT redistribute them verbatim, do NOT copy the .github/workflows generation code; the pipeline design (which sources merged, weekly refresh cadence, ID-mapping approach) is usable at the method level; caveat — ECR is scraped from FantasyPros, whose own ToS needs separate review if ECR becomes load-bearing on a revenue surface.

nflverse/nflverse-pfr verdict: CODE — study-only for the R scraper code (no fork, no copied .R files, no line-by-line R→TypeScript translation since a mechanical translation is still a derivative work); get the snap-count and PFR advanced-stat datasets from nflverse-data releases (CC-BY-4.0) instead.

sumedhk0/PanopticPigskin verdict: CODE — the strongest copyleft in the set, method-only full stop (not the library, not the scripts, not the viewer, and do NOT run it server-side for user-facing outputs under AGPL §13); learnable techniques are (a) calibrate panning/tilting/zooming broadcast cameras from field paint, (b) use known player height to resolve the paint-alone lens ambiguity, (c) per-frame solve plus refinement pass, (d) cross-check the solve against the play's line of scrimmage, (e) endzone camera on its own paint.

nflverse/nflverse-pbp verdict: CC-BY-4.0 is not copyleft — usable with attribution including adaptation of the R scraper logic into a proprietary codebase (no source-sharing, no share-alike); the LICENSE.md is stock CC-BY-4.0 with no code carve-out covering the whole repo and a "code per-repo" check found no per-file alternate license; stripping the attribution is the entire price of this license.

mkreiser/ESPN-Fantasy-Football-API verdict: LIBRARY-SAFE — it is a JavaScript npm package (correction to the sweep note that called it Python); safe to npm install and import unmodified as a dependency, but do NOT copy src/ into the monorepo and do NOT fork-and-vendor a modified copy; the verdict is "safe to depend on," not "must use" — evaluate whether existing intakes already cover it.

Attribution formats from the verdicts: nflverse — "NFL play-by-play, player stats, rosters, schedules, snap counts, and advanced stats via nflverse (https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data), © nflverse contributors, licensed under CC-BY-4.0"; dynastyprocess/data — no attribution is legally required for extracted facts, but provenance is good practice ("ECR/ADP figures cross-referenced against DynastyProcess data, GPL-3.0; values independently stored").

The public/private surface doctrine (Garrett, 2026-09-28 — HARD): the public website shows ONLY projections and rankings (and published picks with their outcomes); the underlying data, metrics, signals, and methodology stay 100% internal — never on a public page, API response, doc, copy, or agent-readable surface.

The doctrine's keep-out list: raw data rows and feeds; metric values and names beyond what a projection implies (EPA, QBR, WOPR, target share, separation); signal values and identifiers (signal ledger, weak-signal registry, calibration internals); methodology (frameworks, factor lists, weights, aggregation formulas, model internals, source registries, "how we read the numbers" write-ups); data sources — which are used AND which were refused, the latter being competitive intel.

The fence pattern already in the repo: apps/web/lib/fences/no-raw-ngs-fence.ts implements a FencePlugin (block/pass) matching restricted patterns in text, payload, and metadata; guardrail scripts trust-gate.mjs, model-freeze.mjs, and draft-only.mjs gate unauthorized state changes in build paths; readiness gates (canExposePerformanceStats, PUBLISH_LEDGER, canPublishProjections) are the structural precedent, with the proof ledger route inheriting honesty from loadLedgerView() as the template for a gate that cannot leak by construction.

The /methodology page currently states "The framework is public; weights, constants, and aggregation formula stay proprietary" — under the doctrine the framework itself goes internal too, because the public side keeps what the projections are, never how they are made.

nflverse data is openly licensed (CC-BY-4.0 with attribution), so showing it is not a legal exposure the way NGS would be — but it is pulled behind the fence anyway, because the website's surface rule is product posture, not just legal posture.

The rankings program defines three products from the same projection core (differing in aggregation and horizon): rest-of-season rankings (projected fantasy value for remaining weeks, by position, weekly Tuesday publish after waivers settle), week-by-week rankings (projected fantasy points for the upcoming week, Wednesday publish, frozen Thursday AM), and positional boards (QB/RB/WR/TE with tier breaks), starting week 4 and continuing through the fantasy playoffs.

Every weekly rankings publish is an immutable snapshot {season, week, product, generated_at, input_hashes, model_version} — never edited in place; material corrections (late injury news, source corrections) ship as new snapshots with a changelog entry {old_snapshot, new_snapshot, changed_players, reason}, and the changelog is part of the product making the accuracy scoreboard auditable.

Hard rule: the rankings never maintain a separate projection fork — one projection core, three presentation aggregations; a divergence between the engine's pick and the published ranking for the same player/week is a bug, not a feature.

The "hand-graded every play" problem decomposed: automatable = a play-tagging pipeline over legally available film (personnel, formation, coverage shell, route concepts, blitz identification), automated QC (cross-tag consistency checks, anomaly flags on physically implausible tags), and diff-against-source with low-confidence tags as the review queue; genuinely human = ambiguous coverage rotations and disguised shells, the QC queue subset, and edge-case adjudication feeding back as training labels; no "hand-graded" claim until humans actually graded.

Internal accuracy tracking for rankings: MAE/RMSE/Spearman vs actuals per position per week, scored automatically after games finalize, with confidence intervals on differences and misses recorded honestly — the internal record, while the public benchmarks are the arena.

Status per the 2026-10-01 audit: the rankings program is QUEUED — NOT BUILT, NOT LIVE — with no implementing code, no API route, and no page; it is foundation-gated (projection source lock + adjustment layer v1 + populated player signals) and rankings without a locked projection source are decoration.

asonty/ngs_highlights open NGS tracking TSVs (2017–2019 seasons, play_data/ per-playKey) carry the full NGS column set (gameId, playId, playType, season, week, quarter, down, yardsToGo, yardline, playDirection, frame, displayName, esbId, gsisId, jerseyNumber, nflId, position, time, x, y, s, o, dir, event, playDescription); key finding — the TSVs contain the entire runtime of the play including dead time before line set and post-TD celebration, so the loader must trim to the play window; dir = 0 faces the far sideline, clockwise (standard NGS convention).

The NGS feed target schema: one row per entity per frame with 23 entities (22 players + BALL), grouping keys game_id → play_id → frame_id at 10 Hz; frame columns include x,y in yards (x in [0,120], y in [0,53.3]), s,a (speed yd/s, acceleration yd/s²), dis (cumulative distance), o,dir (orientation, direction of motion in degrees), event (ball_snap, pass_forward, pass_arrived, possibly null), team (off/def/ball), ball_landing_x/y and frames_to_landing as conditioning anchors; play context carries quarter, down, yards_to_go, yardline_100, seconds_remaining, score_diff, and play_direction canonicalized to "right"; every row or play carries feed metadata (source in {asonty, nfl_ngs_raw, broadcast_cv, licensed, synthetic}, acquired_at, feed_version, valid, identity_keys nflId/gsisId/esbId).

Storage contract from the tracking playbook: raw frames land as per-play Parquet in the lake (lake/tracking/season=YYYY/week=WW/game_id/play_id.parquet) while Postgres holds derived per-play features only — never raw frames — with a one-way boundary (intake writes raw, reshape reads raw, reshape never writes back into the raw tree).

The four data-QC doctrines adopted from nfl-ngs-raw (method only): raw-first (scrape-only contract, raw JSON committed, reshape owned by a separate stage); validity-by-content (presence ≠ validity — a payload is trusted only if it parses AND has rows); pace-between-attempts (sleep after EVERY attempt, success or failure, in a finally — env-tuned with NGS_RAW_SLEEP default 0.25s, NGS_RAW_TIMEOUT default 30s, NGS_RAW_RETRIES default 4; retry {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}; persistent non-404 failures raise, get counted, and turn the stage red); empty-envelope sentinel (HTTP 200 with an empty body or stats: [] means "nothing here" — never banked, and future weeks are never requested because banking an empty envelope would make a presence-based resume skip the real data forever).

Movement-model physics gates: test_no_teleport requires hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 12.0·Δt + 0.5 for every player/horizon; test_speed_cap requires predicted speed ≤ 12.0 yd/s; test_permutation_invariance requires permuting the 22 player input rows to permute outputs identically (<1e-5, no entity positional encoding); test_determinism requires identical seeds to give max abs diff <1e-6; test_causality requires zeroing frames with frame_id > t to leave outputs unchanged (<1e-6).

Uncertainty calibration gates (mandatory before downstream use): ECE_regression = Σ_b (n_b/N)·|RMSE_b − σ̄_b| over 10 equal-count bins of σ̄ = sqrt(0.5·(σx²+σy²)), with the gate ECE < 0.15 yd; coverage at Mahalanobis ≤ 1 (expect 0.393) and ≤ 2 (expect 0.865) for the 2D Gaussian must land within ± 5 pp of nominal; on synthetic data with known σ = 0.5 yd noise the bar is ECE < 0.10 and coverage within ± 3 pp; on failure, apply isotonic recalibration σ_cal = f(σ̄) or temperature-scale logvar' = logvar + log T fit to minimize validation NLL and re-check — if still failing, the module ships point predictions only and the failure is logged, not silently consumed.

RMSE reference yardstick: 0.518–0.540 from the BDB 2026 leaderboard band, computed as sqrt(0.5·(MSE_x + MSE_y)) in yards — directional only since the data differs, but the only public yardstick; the target is to beat 0.540 on GSE's own held-out games with the Phase 3 ensemble + TTA, documenting the gap to 0.518 as the improvement backlog.

Phase 1 gate: the single relational model must beat the Phase 0 physics baseline RMSE by ≥ 10% on the game-level held-out block (expanding-window splits — train games 1..N−2k, validate N−2k+1..N−k, test the most recent k ≥ 10%, minimum 20 games); the Phase 3 gate requires the 5-seed ensemble + TTA (original + horizontal flip) to improve test RMSE over the single model, with expected gain ~0.005–0.010.
Test-time augmentation variance mixing: σ²_mix = mean(σ²) + var(means).

M5 CV-lane acceptance: on ≥ 50 plays with overlapping coverage, per-player CV-derived positions must agree with Zebra-chip frames within mean error < 1.0 yd and 95th percentile < 2.0 yd; ball interpolation must handle dropped frames without teleporting (passes the no-teleport inequality); production wiring stays gated on counsel clearance or a licensed input via a repo flag, not a comment.

Verified-but-negative findings (do not chase): nflverse publishes NO per-frame tracking data — its NGS product is player-week aggregates (ngs_{passing,receiving,rushing}, CC-BY-4.0), useful only as calibration targets; the public nextgenstats.nfl.com/api surface may be dead (moved behind NFL+ Premium at pro.nfl.com/api/secured/* per a 2026-09-04 SportsDataverse commit); nfl-ngs-raw itself only gets tracking for highlight plays (per-game lookups denied from every egress tested).

Big Data Bowl 2026 license discrepancy: the movement spec (2026-09-26) records the data as CC BY-NC 4.0 with benchmark-only use permitted, while the older tracking playbook (2026-07-02) records the 2026 terms as no-license/confidential with a post-contest data-destruction requirement — these conflict, so resolve by reading the actual current license text before ANY BDB data touches the build; default posture until then is no BDB data at all, not even for benchmarking.

Licensed NGS feed options: SkillCorner (~10fps all-22 tracking keyed to PFF + GSIS IDs, low-to-mid five figures/yr estimate, unquoted — verify via demo, confirm downstream commercial-use license and indemnity); Genius Sports (official Zebra-chip raw feed, exclusive through the 2029 season, prior deal $120M/6yr — six-to-seven-figure conversation); SIS DataHub Pro ($99.99/mo or $749.99/yr self-serve — charting adjunct, not a feed-creation input); never build against a vendor API without a signed license.

Loader normalization rules: trim dead time (drop frames outside the line_set → terminal-event play window); canonicalize playDirection to "right" (horizontal flip once where needed); history window T = 10 frames (1.0 s) ending at t; causality enforced — features may only use frame_id ≤ t; augmentation flips recompute derived kinematics from flipped raw coords and are involutive (test_flip_involution).

The cv-movement-primitive lane reimplements optical-flow camera-motion compensation → yardline homography (pixels → field meters; field 120×53.3 yd = 109.7×48.8 m) → world-coordinate tracklets → per-player speed/distance derivation, plus ball interpolation across dropped frames; it ships no detector weights (the YOLO-class detector is a separate procure-vs-train decision), and DIY extraction on NFL+/broadcast streams is blocked without counsel.

Ledger verdict REJECT (2026-09-21): in Nomura et al. 2025 (arXiv:2504.03353) on decentralized collective world models, the authors' own experiments show the decentralized emergent-communication approach is second-best to centralized models (BC > EC > NC), and the paper's motivating constraint (agents unable to observe full state or each other's representations) does not apply to centralized tracking data.

The decentralized world-model paper approximates the incalculable joint message posterior q(m_t|{s_t^k}) with a Product-of-Experts over per-agent message estimates, combined with bidirectional message exchange and contrastive learning for message alignment; policies were trained by behavioral cloning on expert demos with no RL skill acquisition.

The decentralized paper's Product-of-Experts message approximations (eq. 3): prior p(m_t) approx C times the product over agents of p(m_t^k), and posterior q(m_t|{s_t^k}) approx C times the product over agents of q(m_t^k|s_t^k).
equation: p(m_t) \approx C\prod_k p(m_t^k),\quad q(m_t|\{s_t^k\}) \approx C\prod_k q(m_t^k|s_t^k)

claim: Each agent in the decentralized world-model paper uses an RSSM with representation q(s_t^k|s_{t-1}^k,m_{t-1},a_{t-1}^k,o_t^k), transition p(s_t^k|s_{t-1}^k,m_{t-1},a_{t-1}^k), and observation p(o_t^k|s_t^k), plus a shared message variable m_t.

The decentralized emergent-communication experiments (100 trials per condition on a synthetic two-agent hypotrochoid-drawing task) found minimal differences with vs without communication (overlapping std except at bin=1), and emergent message quality was measured only via RSA (Spearman correlation between message dissimilarity matrices and true trajectory) - a representation diagnostic, not a performance metric.

The REJECT ledger's replacement gate: it stands unless a follow-up shows emergent-communication world models beating centralized aggregation on a >=10-agent continuous-control task with full observability available.

Ledger verdict ADAPT (2026-09-21): Kurach et al. 2020, Google Research Football (arXiv:1907.11180v2) - a physics-based 3D soccer simulator (customized GameplayFootball in C++, full 11v11 rules, default game 3000 frames at 10fps x 5min, ~140M env steps/day on a single hexa-core Intel Xeon W-2135), open-source at github.com/google-research/football; no NFL-transferable model, but two portable ideas: non-transitive evaluation and spatial mini-map encodings for tracking data.

Google Research Football's Checkpoint reward shapes the opponent half into 10 regions by Euclidean distance to goal, paying +0.1 for first controlled possession in each region (max +1 = one goal), with uncollected checkpoints credited on scoring and each credited once per episode.

GRF benchmark baselines (mean average goal difference over 5 seeds, 500M steps): with the Checkpoint reward, IMPALA reached easy 12.83 +/- 1.30, medium 5.54 +/- 0.90, hard 3.15 +/- 0.37; with Scoring reward, DQN reached easy 8.16 +/- 1.05, medium 2.01 +/- 0.27, hard 0.27 +/- 0.56 - checkpoint shaping massively helped policy-gradient methods while DQN performed similarly under both rewards.

GRF representation experiment (IMPALA + Checkpoint on easy 11v11, 500M steps): stacked Super Mini Map 12.89 +/- 0.51 beat raw SMM 9.75 +/- 4.15, gray pixels 7.18 +/- 0.85, and compact floats 5.73 +/- 0.28 - hand-designed spatial encodings beat both raw pixels and coordinate vectors.

GRF self-play non-transitivity result (Table 2): agent B beats agent A 11.93 +/- 2.19, agent A beats the built-in medium AI 4.25 +/- 1.72, yet agent B loses to the same bot -0.27 +/- 0.33 - the portable caution being that pairwise model bake-offs can misrank candidates, so selection should use a fixed benchmark suite plus Elo-style rating.

GRF multi-agent experiment (3v1-with-Keeper, 50M steps): controlling 1 player scored 0.68 +/- 0.03, 2 players 0.81 +/- 0.17, 3 players 0.86 +/- 0.08 - slower start with more controlled players, higher ceiling.

Ledger verdict ADAPT (2026-09-21): Bhaskar et al. 2024, Node Classification With Integrated Reject Option (arXiv:2412.03190v1) - the portable artifact is the cost-based (K+1)-class reject loss, which is backbone-agnostic and applies to any classifier with a softmax output; the GNN node-classification framing itself is not sports-relevant.

The cost-based reject loss (Eq. 1) treats 'reject' as the (K+1)-th class: l_ce^d = -log f_y(h) - (1-d)*log f_{K+1}(h); small d makes the model prefer rejection and d=1 reduces to standard cross-entropy, and it is consistent with the l_{0d1} loss (Cao et al. 2022).

The coverage-based reject formulation (NCwR-Cov, SelectiveNet-style): selective risk r(f,g|S_n) = [(1/n) sum l(f(h_i),y_i) g(h_i)] / phi(g|S_n), empirical coverage phi(g|S_n) = (1/n) sum g(h_i), objective E(f,g) = r(f,g|S_n) + lambda*Psi(c - phi(g|S_n)) with Psi(a) = max(0,a)^2 and lambda=32, final loss E = alpha*E(f,g) + (1-alpha)*E(f) with alpha=0.5.

Headline empirical finding: NCwR-Cost beats Softmax-Response thresholding at all coverage levels on Cora/Citeseer/Pubmed and beats CF-GNN everywhere except Cora at 50% coverage and Pubmed below 60% coverage; cost-based dominates coverage-based because the cost loss rejects hard/boundary examples first (t-SNE: rejected points sit in class-overlap regions) while the coverage constraint rejects arbitrary examples (sometimes whole classes, e.g. classes 3-4 at 50.4% coverage).

Exact numbers: Cora with d=0.5 reached 95.8 +/- 0.05 accuracy at 42.6 +/- 0.02 coverage (d=1: 81.65 at 100% coverage); Citeseer d=0.5: 91.6 +/- 0.12 at 9.7 +/- 0.05 coverage; ILDC d=0.25: 87.24 +/- 2.45 accuracy at 67.00 +/- 3.30 coverage; ILDC NCwR-Cov at 0.5 coverage: 97.55 +/- 0.62.

Validation setup: 10 random initializations, mean +/- std accuracy on unrejected test samples at fixed coverage levels; baselines Softmax Response (reject when max softmax below thresholds 0.5-0.9) and CF-GNN (reject when predicted label set has >1 class); standard splits of 20 nodes per class for training, 500 validation, 1000 test on Cora/Citeseer/Pubmed; NCwR-Cov shows high variance in the authors' own note (unstable coverage-penalty optimization).

The ADAPT ledger's GSE-facing lesson: price the abstention, don't fix the coverage - i.e. set the reject cost d from economics rather than constraining coverage, with the gate being >=8% higher backtested profit than the best post-hoc confidence-threshold rule at the same abstain rate (abstain rate <= 30%) on a validation season.

The desk's daily-floor argument: daily index volatility is about 70 basis points versus equity drift of about 4 basis points on a 10% year, so half a quiet day of noise is larger than a year of drift divided by 252 — for any long-equity book sized so that $300 is the mean, the hit rate on 'today's mark >= $300' stays near a coin flip.

The Zakamouline efficient-hedging approximation (Zakamouline 2006; coefficients as printed by Sinclair and implemented in sweliam/zakamouline.py getH0/getH1/getK; a numerical fit to the Hodges-Neuberger utility hedge, not a theorem): H0 = λ / (γ S σ² T), where λ is proportional cost, γ is risk aversion (not Black-Scholes gamma), and Γ is Black-Scholes gamma.
The H1 piece of the Zakamouline no-transaction band: H1 = 1.12 λ^0.31 T^0.05 (e^(−rT) / σ)^0.25 (|Γ| / γ)^0.5.
K is negative: long options get a lower modified vol σ_m² = σ² (1 + K) and short options get a higher σ_m² = σ² (1 − K); hedge to the nearest band delta(σ_m) ± (H0 + H1), not to flat delta.
The Whalley-Wilmott 1997 half-width is (1.5 e^(−rT) λ S Γ² / γ)^(1/3), a looser comparator to the Zakamouline band.
Leland 1985's k uses the rehedge interval δt, not expiry T: k = sqrt(2/π) λ / (σ sqrt(δt)); the prior desk note wrongly put T in that slot and centered the band on Leland instead of on K.
Charm at r=0, q=0, ATM reduces to −n(d1) σ / (4 √T) ≈ −0.056 per year, about −0.00015 of delta per calendar day; the prior note's −0.198 is not this formula and must not be hedged off.

Dollar gamma per 1% move = Γ × OI × 100 × S² × 0.01 × sign (customer-long sign −1 on every contract); dollar vanna VEX = vanna × OI × 100 × S × 0.01 × sign with vanna = e^(−qT) n(d1) d2 / σ; measured on the 2026-09-24 SPY snapshot at S=766.82: customer-long GEX −$43.80B per 1%, squeeze GEX −$2.58B, customer-long VEX +$588M per +1 vol point, CHEX −$4.88M per calendar day.

Under the customer-long sign convention there is no flip strike: the GEX sum is negative at every strike, so a cumulative walk cannot cross zero; under the squeeze convention the cumulative walk inside ±$80 of spot was still about −$1.9B at the top of the window and −$11.2B at 766 — it did not cross zero.

The charter's three-rung validation doctrine: Rung 1 DESCRIPTIVE (a signal is computed as-of and logged, no test — every signal with a reachable source starts here immediately, because a signal deferred today is sample that never exists); Rung 2 PREDICTIVE (it beats a NAMED dumb baseline at predicting the settled outcome, out of sample, on fixture-grouped folds, with the kill line pre-registered before the run and NO market term anywhere — clearing it means the signal is REAL and enters the engine as a component permanently); Rung 3 PRICEABLE (it adds skill over the market with the market logit as a FIXED OFFSET, coefficient pinned at 1 and unpenalized — only rung-2 survivors are ever tested there, which shrinks the multiple-testing family by an order of magnitude and makes the FDR budget affordable; clearing it sizes a position, failing it demotes nothing).

Charter corollary: test at the layer with the most labels — pick-level labels number in the thousands while play-level, drive-level and player-game labels number in the hundreds of thousands to millions; testing a novel signal at pick level with n=2,600 against the hardest benchmark is how ten months disappeared.

Validating signals by asking 'does this beat the closing line?' structurally cannot credit anything new: a freshly engineered statistic has never been priced by anyone, including its creators, so market-relative regression on it returns noise, not zero; with ~2,600 settled picks the residual sample is tiny so the noise wins and the signal dies. DVOA in 2003 would have failed that test; it earned its place by predicting outcomes better than the alternatives of its day, and when the market caught up its market edge went to zero while its value as a component did not.

The 10Hz paper's capital-gate likelihood ratio is upside down: the paper defines M_t as the market likelihood over the model likelihood and unlocks execution when M_t is large — but under H0 ('outcomes ~ market') that statistic grows exactly when the market explains outcomes better than the model does, so it unlocks capital when there is no edge; the repo's forecast-skill-eprocess.ts has it the right way round.

||a(t)|| < 0 is physically impossible — the Euclidean norm of acceleration cannot be negative — so the paper's break-point detection as written never fires; the correct test is path-wise deceleration a · v < 0.

ESOE = S(t_arrival) − E[S(t_arrival)|…] is separation-over-expected, not 'expected separation over expected'; its conditioning set includes t_throw − t_break, so it does not isolate receiver skill from QB timing as the paper claims.

Adaptive Conformal Inference is four lines of arithmetic adapting to drift: alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma*(alpha - err_t); it needs nothing new, and 'adaptive-conformal' was missing from the repo.

The Jackknife+ coverage floor is 1-2alpha, never 1-alpha: report the field as coverageFloor, never guaranteedCoverage, and scope is MARGINAL. The '2' comes from the n+1 leave-one-out residual comparison, not two Gaussian tails. Fail-closed order stats: at n=5, alpha=0.1 the interval is plus/minus infinity; finiteIntervalMinN(0.1)=9. Typical coverage hugs 1-alpha, which is the misreport trap.

2023 Nex Theorem 5: the coverage bound under distribution drift is P(cover) >= 1-2alpha minus the weighted total-variation terms. Omitting the drift terms does NOT print d_i=0; use exponential rho weights.
The bounded drift coverage gap formula is boundedDriftCoverageGap(epsilon,rho)=2*epsilon/(1-rho), where epsilon is the caller's; the fleet does not invent an NFL weekly epsilon.

claim: The walk-forward embargo is bypassable: the synthetic group row uses decisionAt from the FIRST member while the embargo test reads that single timestamp, so a group with an earlier first member and a later member inside the embargo window is never marked embargoed, and train = fold.train.flatMap((g) => g.members) puts every member (including the in-embargo one) into train. The as-of guard passes on unreadable clocks: Date.getTime() is NaN for an Invalid Date and NaN > NaN is false, so the guard returns CLEAN and an unreadable clock walks through the lookahead tripwire. Non-finite ms must be rejected first by throwing SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError (a clock you cannot read is a source that cannot speak as-of).

The empty fold discards the market offset: `if (n === 0) return () => 0.5;` in logistic.ts throws away the fixed market-logit offset and reports a coin flip, which then feeds rung-3 comparisons. An empty training fold must return sigmoid(readOffset({ offset })) instead.

Adversarial verification of e1c5334: all four fixes are correct. asof-guard.ts applies Number.isFinite to both ms values and throws SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError (a clock you cannot read is a source that cannot speak as-of, not a source that spoke late); walk-forward.ts got a 49-line fixture-grouping regression test; logistic.ts no longer discards the offset on empty folds.

A measured correlation caveat with an operating rule from anytime-ledger.ts: markets on one game share the outcome and break independence. A mixture-copula at rho 0.5 and two perfectly-correlated markets per game stay at or under 0.05 type-I error (0.036), but THREE perfectly-correlated markets per game inflates type-I error to 0.11. Stated rule: feed at most ONE pick per game. calibration-sequence.ts is flagged as more fragile, up to 5x.

Replacement for the killed latency arbitrage: PRE-MOVEMENT ALERT. The same B-spline curvature spike a syndicate would use to hit a stale book is delivered to a subscriber 30-90 seconds before the rest of the market reprices; this attacks the ESTABLISHED blocker directly (CLV beat-close 23.0% vs the 52.4% requirement) since a subscriber who wagers before the steam completes beats the close by construction. No 400ms needed, no execution layer.

Replacement for the killed streaming-GPU tier: EVENT-DRIVEN RECOMPUTE. When the curvature detector fires on a game, recompute THAT game only, on the existing serverless path, at zero GPU cost. Same principle (react to the state transition rather than poll), at GSE's scale. Picks are currently minted on a cron schedule against odds that may be hours old.

claim: Barber et al. (2020) is a hard limit on the product: distribution-free confidence intervals of bounded length for a binary conditional probability are impossible without structural assumptions, so no bounded per-pick uncertainty band can ever be honestly published — any per-pick interval is either unbounded or assumption-laden, and the honest move is to name the exchangeability assumption on the surface itself.

Jackknife+ gives 1-2*alpha coverage, not 1-alpha: at alpha=0.10 it guarantees 80% coverage, not 90%. It remains the right tool for NFL n~70 because it wastes no sample on a calibration split, but claiming 90% off a 1-2*alpha guarantee is the same 'fake tightness' the paper attacks.

The team has never measured its own data-corruption rate despite known corruption (fixture triplication with three game rows per NFL fixture, phantom fixtures absent from ESPN's schedule, consensusPct pinned at exactly 1.0000 on every MLB run line, a three-week line-archive outage nobody alarmed on). The one-evening job: define physical-plausibility bounds nothing real can violate (de-vigged two-way probabilities summing outside [0.98, 1.06]; an NFL total outside [24, 70]; a moneyline implying < 0.5% or > 99.5%; consensusPct exactly 1.0 on a market whose line is structurally constant) and count violations; the kill line is that a violation rate under 1% makes the gate not worth building, and the stated on-the-record prediction is above 5%.

For steam detection, invert the paper's own advice: reject Hawkes (it needs a fitted intensity mu/alpha/beta, and fitting a self-exciting process on weeks of archive fits noise) and use its unfitted geometric detector instead — apply Cox-de Boor B-splines to the odds time series with instantaneous curvature, where a steam move is a global curvature maximum plus an immediate velocity deceleration; zero parameters to fit, works on thin data. The Rung-2 kill line is no improvement in predicting the closing line's direction over a simple price-delta-per-time threshold on 200+ archived movements.

State-transition cost principle: when a defender's hip-orientation mismatch exceeds 90 degrees he must hip-flip and his acceleration drops near zero for 200-400ms — a forced state transition has a cost in time during which the agent cannot respond. The market analogue: after a genuine steam move, books reprice at different speeds, so the edge is in measuring cross-book price dispersion in the seconds AFTER a curvature spike rather than the dispersion at rest (this depends on the curvature detector landing first).

STEAM-CURVATURE build spec: cubic B-spline over the odds time series with an RTS (Rauch-Tung-Striebel) forward-backward smoother FIRST so the second derivative does not amplify bid-ask bounce, then instantaneous curvature; a steam move is a global curvature maximum plus an immediate velocity deceleration. Pure function, no DB writes, no gate; build and test on synthetic paths with known injected curvature first, then run over the 2026-08-19..08-22 window (684,498 odds_line_snapshot rows, the only real archive) as the real-data check.

VENN-WIDTH-MEASURE spec: measure the actual Venn-Abers interval width on the engine's settled picks using the existing ivapPredict/cvapPredict — report the delta-p distribution deciles, the share above 0.20, and the shares above whatever threshold would veto 5/10/20% of published rows, stratified by sport and book count; the deliverable is a measurement document plus harness, NOT a wired gate, so the founder can pick a threshold backed by the team's own rows.

The standing implementation rule: before implementing ANY named method from a paper, git grep the CODE (not docs/) for its name — the author re-derived Shin after it had already been measured and declined on 621 settled picks on 2026-09-13, with the answer sitting in a comment in pick-proof-receipt.ts, and three of the four blueprint methods in the dispatch were already built.

Law 3 boundary held on the width gate: setting maxWidthForFire from undefined to 0.20 flips a gate, which no agent does unilaterally; the correct move is to measure the width distribution and hand the founder a threshold backed by the team's own rows instead of the paper's unsourced 0.20.

Empirical Jackknife+ coverage sits near 1-alpha in practice, not at the 1-2alpha floor: 4,000 trials per cell on exchangeable Gaussian data at alpha=0.10 gave empirical coverage 0.9030/0.9042/0.9045 at n=9/20/50 against a floor of 0.80 — which is precisely why the 1-2alpha misreport is universal.

The Jackknife+ module's fail-closed design: upperOrderStat returns POSITIVE_INFINITY when k > n instead of clamping ('Fail-closed, never clamped'), and the module should carry a boundedness-direction field (none/lower/upper/both) plus minimumNForFiniteInterval on each result so a caller can tell which rank fell outside [1, n] for the refusal census and how many more settled rows are needed for a finite interval.

Steam-curvature measurement: the RTS retrospective smoother is a lookahead probe, not causal — normalized |velocity| read 0.3 and 0.1 causally versus 5.3 and 5.6 retrospectively two samples BEFORE the jump. The correct deceleration statistic is a dot v < 0, never |a| < 0, and graph curvature peaks in the settled tail rather than at the jump; the shipped causal-vs-retrospective tests prove the causal estimate at index k does not move when a later sample changes.

The last three CI runs on main all failed on 'Test, type-check, lint, Prisma', and because the PR branch was cut from a failing commit, the failure is inherited by every branch, taxing every agent. The reported 740-of-1040 vitest failures were an invocation artifact: the @/ path alias is defined in apps/web's own vitest config and resolves relative to apps/web, so running vitest from the repo root fails every @/ import at collection time (740 files failed to load, not an assertion failure); CI runs each workspace in its own directory and does not have this alias problem, so the CI failure is a genuine failure, possibly a suite that grew past its step-level timeout.

The climatology-gate design got right: a three-valued verdict (kill / survive / UNDERPOWERED, where underpowered at n < MIN_N is never a pass), BSS <= 0 kills so a model exactly equaling the dummy is killed, no market term in the header, outcomes applied after probabilities are recorded, and shadow pricing with no publish. The criticism: p=0.5 is honestly weak because NFL home teams win roughly 55-57%, so a no-skill constant 'say 0.57 for the home side' would survive; the third option is a frozen prior-season home-win constant as the kill baseline (not noisy, not trivially beatable, pre-registerable, as-of clean), i.e. BSS vs the frozen prior-season rate > 0 at n >= 100.

Measured why the 1-2alpha Jackknife+ misreport is universal: with 4,000 trials per cell, exchangeable draws, a leave-one-out constant predictor, and alpha 0.10, empirical coverage was 0.9030 (n=9), 0.9042 (n=20), 0.9045 (n=50) against a proved floor of 0.80. Because Jackknife+ is conservative, its typical coverage lands right on 1-alpha, so sanity-checkers read 0.90 and write 0.90 on the label; a threshold tuned to the empirical figure is tuned to luck, since the theorem only guarantees coverage no worse than 1-2alpha.

The trust gate rejected the field name guaranteedCoverage under banned.guaranteed-outcome and was right: the theorem proves coverage is no worse than 1-2alpha, so the accurate name is coverageFloor ('floor' states the guarantee where the rejected word lets a reader hear an equality); the rule is to reword the source, never the guard, and never add allowlist entries when it fires.

A Jackknife+ result carries a refusedBound field ('none' | 'lower' | 'upper' | 'both') because a caller reading the result object otherwise cannot tell which rank fell outside [1, n]; for the refusal census, 'we refused' and 'we refused the upper bound because n was too small for this alpha' are different rows, and only the second tells an operator what to change.

The ranking premise was corrected: the board does not sort on confidence. rankingSortKey prefers factorBreakdown.rankingP when finite, falls back to rankingScore/100, and reaches confidence only when both are absent; rankingP (n=1,390) is monotone while confidence (n=2,385) is inverted, so the anti-predictive score drives order only on rows that fall all the way through. readRankingKey returning {basis,key} is now the single branch decision, with rankingSortKey a thin wrapper and key equality pinned on 15 cases.

The typecheck root-cause fix: SignalFamily was a 6-member union while three packages already used 8; the fix widened the union to match the eight keys of DEFAULT_FAMILY_PRIOR_WEIGHTS (MARKET .28, EFFICIENCY .22, TRENCHES .14, SITUATIONAL .12, MICROCLIMATE .08, MARKET_MICROSTRUCTURE .06, LUCK .05, NARRATIVE .05, summing to 1.00) rather than merging, deliberately, because family is what the agreement computation clusters on and folding MICROCLIMATE into SITUATIONAL would manufacture phantom consensus by counting one source twice.

SignalCategory is a different concept from signal family and must not be widened to match call sites: it is fourteen data-source kinds (ODDS, SCHEDULE, WEATHER, INJURIES, RATINGS, MARKET_SENTIMENT, PLAYER_AVAILABILITY, OFFICIALS, VENUE_ENVIRONMENT, TEAM_RATES, STANDINGS, DIVISION_CONTEXT, MILESTONES, PACE) mirroring the Prisma enum and the database contract; widening the local type would let the type permit values the database cannot store, the precise defect class behind a three-week line-archive outage.

All three CLV rates were surfaced with their own denominators (decided 0.4084 n=901, all-graded 0.2319 n=1587, push 0.4323 n=1587) by design, refusing a directive to report only the flattering reading; and a number discrepancy was flagged: the directive cites 370/911 and 370/1616 while read-only SELECT measured 368/901 and 368/1587, 29 rows apart, most likely a later snapshot or different filter.

The Kit lead-list generator finds local service businesses with zero-key data: Nominatim geocodes the city to a bounding box, then Overpass queries OSM with exact key=value tag matches only (craft/trade/shop/office), deliberately avoiding regex because public Overpass mirrors 504 on it, failing over across three mirrors (private.coffee, overpass-api.de, kumi.systems) and widening the search radius from 30 km to 45 km once if short of the limit.

The lead-scoring rubric scores prospects 0-100 by web-presence weakness: 85-100 for no findable website (best prospects), 70-84 for a listed but dead site, 40-69 for a live but weak site (http-only, directory or social-page URL), 10-39 for a solid live site; a listed site returning HTTP 403 is treated as bot-blocking rather than dead, scored 60-69 and flagged for manual verification, and small +/- adjustments are added for tag completeness (phone, full address).

When OSM has no website tag, the script cross-checks the keyless DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint before concluding a business has no site, discarding ads and directory domains and matching the candidate URL against the business name's non-stopword tokens (length >= 5) to decide whether it is the business's own site.

An audit of the ORB v4 0DTE options plan computes expectancy per trade from the cited (not re-measured) 41.25% win rate and 1.99 payoff (average win divided by average loss): 0.4125 x 1.99 - 0.5875 = 0.233 loss-units, i.e. the plan is negative-expectancy as stated.

ledger_writer.py's consecutive_losses(day) counts the trailing streak of POSITION_CLOSED entries with pnl < 0, resetting the streak to 0 on any non-negative close, and returns 0 when the day's ledger file does not exist.

The paper's CRPS kill line is inverted and statistically empty: it states a measurable improvement of less than 0.01 on 150 settled spreads while Rung 2 demands demonstrably beating the baseline, opposite directions. Measured power: the closed-form Gaussian CRPS has calibrated expectation sigma/sqrt(pi); with NFL score-margin sigma ~= 14 points, E[CRPS] = 7.90, a 0.01 improvement is 0.13% relative, the SE of the mean at n=150 is 0.454, so 0.01 is 0.022 standard errors, and detecting a 0.01 delta at 95% would require about 1.2 million samples. Direction: lower CRPS is better; 0.5 points is about 6% of the 7.9 baseline, about 1.1 SE at n=272 unpaired; 0.01 is forbidden.

Brier is the CRPS of a Bernoulli: replacing all Brier tracking for continuous margins is fine, but replacing Brier for moneylines is not. The paper's claim that Brier is incapable of evaluating continuous spreads is wrong as applied to spread covers, which are binary and are Brier-scored today.

Shin de-vigging re-solved from the quadratic (Cain/Clarke implementation of Shin 1992/93): proportional devigging UNDER-weights favourites and over-weights longshots; Shin moves probability mass AWAY from the midpoint; removing more vig from the longshot lowers the longshot and raises the favourite. On a symmetric book, prop = shin = 0.5 with z ~= 0.048, an identity that confirms a working solver. The solved z values of 0.032-0.048 match the 3-5% insider fraction reported in horse-racing literature. The repo's edge-lab/devig.ts already states the correct direction and its unit tests assert the favourite comes in above proportional; the paper has the direction backwards.
