Jackknife+ interval-width arithmetic confirmed and its implication reframed: at NFL margin sigma 13.8, an 80% interval is +/-17.7 points; interval width is set by sigma, not by the conformal method, so a split-conformal 80% interval on ten thousand nflverse margins is also about +/-18. Every honest 80% NFL margin interval is +/-18 because football is that noisy; switching methods never narrows it, only a better mean does. Spreads must be priced from the tail integral, never from interval membership: at sigma 13.8 on a 3-point spread, model mean edges of 0, 1, 2, 3 points give P(cover) of 0.4140, 0.4424, 0.4711, 0.5000.

Curvature is the wrong statistic for a time-indexed odds series: curvature = |p''|/(1+p'^2)^{3/2}, so the (1+p'^2) denominator suppresses exactly the fast segment a steam move is, while the settled tail where p' goes to 0 reads as high curvature. On the synthetic shape, causal argmax |acceleration| = index 9 (the jump, correct) versus argmax curvature = index 17 (the flat tail, wrong). Curvature measures turning per unit arc length for a path through space, but a price-vs-time graph has two axes with unrelated units, so it mostly reports slope; maxCurvatureIndex now ships in every result so the divergence stays visible.

The steam-detection rule was honestly left unbuilt: converting the statistics into a verdict needs a deceleration window and a ratio, picking them needs labelled real steam events, the archive has only four days, and a threshold fitted to one synthetic path is a curve fit with one point, so both thresholds are required options with no defaults and the rule is explicitly marked unbuilt.

Node budgets do not bound time: per-node cost grows with pool size, so with all four runs stopping on the same 400k nodes, 50 players took 2.3s, 100 players 10.6s, 150 players 24.1s, and 200 players 43.8s, a 19x time spread at identical node count. The fix is costBudget = work x pool size with default 600M, giving 1.3-2.0s at every size from 50 to 600 players with the best value identical to the unbounded run. Generalise: any budget you add anywhere must be checked to see that its unit actually tracks the cost you care about.

Decoupling premise: running a live 10Hz micro-movement spatial tracking pipeline costs enterprise licensing typically exceeding hundreds of thousands of dollars annually; Big Data Bowl is CC BY-NC 4.0 and scraping token-gated NextGenStats endpoints for commercial use violates non-commercial licenses and terms of service; and parsing raw coordinate feeds needs zero-copy IPC plus dedicated GPU inference clusters (Apache Arrow Flight, NVIDIA Triton) to hold sub-20 millisecond latency. The sanctioned path is open-source play-by-play data (nflverse), point-in-time public aggregates, and non-commercial tracking data used strictly for offline method validation.

Data-integrity finding: audits of raw sports event logs indicate approaching 19% of frames in some spatial datasets contain state-transition inconsistencies, impossible telemetry, or corrupted formatting. The mandated physical-plausibility gate sits at the ingestion edge: flag any player movement exceeding 13 meters per second as fatally corrupt, reject non-finite timestamps as sources that cannot speak as-of (SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError), and scan for fixture triplication, phantom matches from API timeouts, and market consensus pinned at exactly 1.0000.

Density-migration doctrine: legacy point probabilities price exactly one line and obscure bimodal outcomes; the architecture mandates migration to full margin densities, because one predicted density prices every alternate spread, alternate total, and teaser simultaneously and is the only mathematically sound way to price middles and find where the market's full probability curve diverges from fair value.

CRPS as the primary proper scoring rule for margins: it generalizes absolute error to full predictive distributions by integrating the squared distance between the forecast CDF and the empirical step function at the realized outcome, penalizing models that fail to capture true variance. For Gaussian forecasts the closed-form CRPS uses the standard normal CDF Phi and PDF phi at z = (y - mu)/sigma, letting the engine score hundreds of thousands of hypothetical margin densities against historical settlements in milliseconds.

Fake-tightness audit: at 90% nominal coverage (alpha=0.10) with n=5, clamping the conformal rank to the maximum available sample reports 90% confidence while the true finite-sample coverage is 83.33%, so downstream execution gates misprice risk with false confidence. The mandated policy is fail-closed: ban all quantile clamping, return infinite intervals or issue a definitive refusal when the sample cannot mathematically support the requested coverage.

Jackknife+ for scarce samples: with a full NFL season yielding only n ~= 70 relevant head-to-head analogs, burning half the data on a split conformal calibration set is devastating, so the engine uses leave-one-out fitted models and LOO residuals. The corrected guarantee is 1-2alpha, not 1-alpha: at alpha=0.10 the interval carries exactly 80% guaranteed coverage, and the system must report this to avoid reintroducing fake tightness.

Barber et al. (2020) limit: creating bounded-length, distribution-free confidence intervals for binary conditional probabilities is mathematically impossible without structural assumptions. The protocol names the exchangeability assumption explicitly on the product surface and replaces single point estimates for binary sides with Generalized Venn-Abers calibration, fitting dual monotonic isotonic regressions with PAVA on calibration data augmented with both hypothetical test labels to produce exact multiprobability bounds [p0, p1]. If the epistemic width Delta_p exceeds 0.20, the engine fails closed and refuses to produce a forecast.

Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI): under distribution drift from weather transitions, roster churn, and coaching adaptation, ACI monitors empirical coverage error online and updates the nominal miscoverage level alpha_t immediately after every resolved event via a step-error formula governed by tuning parameter gamma. Sequential under-coverage widens subsequent intervals until nominal coverage is restored, guaranteeing asymptotic coverage without full-model retraining.

Shin devigging: the sportsbook overround is modeled as an asymmetric defense against a modeled fraction of insider trading, not a uniform margin. Solving a quadratic identifies the insider-trading parameter z; Shin devigging disproportionately removes vig from longshot outcomes, shading fair probabilities back toward the midpoint, giving the most accurate reflection of the market's true belief as the unpolluted baseline for the performance model. (Note: the fleet's independent grok verdict re-solved the quadratic and found the paper's stated direction backwards; see the grok blueprint-verdict rows.)

B-spline steam detection: cubic B-spline parameterization gives a twice-differentiable representation of discrete odds shifts, the raw odds sequence is first passed through a Rauch-Tung-Striebel (RTS) Kalman smoother to isolate macro trajectory from bid-ask bounce, and steam is gated on an extreme global maximum in the curvature tensor kappa(t) combined with a localized deceleration dip in velocity. The Hawkes self-exciting process is deprecated for short-horizon odds data because fitting it on weeks of data overfits to high-frequency noise. (Note: the fleet's opus and grok audits flagged RTS as a leakage hole and curvature as the wrong statistic for a 1-D series.)

E-process capital gating: an anytime-valid sequential likelihood-ratio martingale rooted in Ville's inequality continuously tests the engine's probabilistic edge against the Shin-devigged market consensus. Only upon definitively breaching the predefined confidence boundary does the system proceed to execution, with position sizing from worst-case robust Kelly optimization computed over the Venn-Abers epistemic confidence sets.

State-transition cost principle as latency-arbitrage analog: a cornerback reacting to a route break incurs a 200-400 millisecond biomechanical transition penalty (flipping hips, dropping forward acceleration to zero), creating an exploitable separation window; the paper analogizes this to bookmakers' staggered 200-400ms repricing after genuine steam, with stale prices persisting on slower secondary books during the forced state transition. (Note: the fleet's grok verdict killed this section: the 200-400ms figure is borrowed, not measured on bookmaker APIs, and risk-free CLV needs a fill, a latency, and a legal venue the fleet lacks.)
